and helped Holly to report the post."

214
00:11:27.900 --> 00:11:32.700
Amira showed kindness and honesty towards Holly.

215
00:11:32.700 --> 00:11:36.363
She did this by supporting her immediately,

216
00:11:37.710 --> 00:11:41.253
telling Holly that she already knew about the comment,

217
00:11:42.330 --> 00:11:45.183
and helping Holly to report the post.

218
00:11:46.830 --> 00:11:51.210
This means that Holly is more likely to trust Amira,

219
00:11:51.210 --> 00:11:54.063
which is an important feature of a healthy friendship.

220
00:11:57.150 --> 00:12:00.783
How might being in a healthy friendship make someone feel?

221
00:12:02.010 --> 00:12:06.900
Aisha says, "It makes me feel positive and happy."

222
00:12:06.900 --> 00:12:10.797
Andeep says, "I feel safe and confident."

223
00:12:11.970 --> 00:12:15.123
What other feelings might you have in a healthy friendship?

224
00:12:17.640 --> 00:12:20.700
I hope that you've been able to think of a few.

225
00:12:20.700 --> 00:12:21.990
In a healthy friendship,

226
00:12:21.990 --> 00:12:26.990
you might feel valued, accepted, and listened to.

227
00:12:31.890 --> 00:12:34.650
Time for another check for understanding.

228
00:12:34.650 --> 00:12:37.514
Who is describing how someone might feel

229
00:12:37.514 --> 00:12:39.303
in a healthy friendship?

230
00:12:40.200 --> 00:12:43.710
Sam says, "Respect for a person's boundaries

231
00:12:43.710 --> 00:12:46.797
is really important in a healthy friendship."

232
00:12:48.000 --> 00:12:51.870
Sofia says, "Kindness is an important feature

233
00:12:51.870 --> 00:12:53.547
of a healthy friendship."

234
00:12:54.720 --> 00:12:57.900
And Alex says, "A healthy friendship

235
00:12:57.900 --> 00:13:01.830
might increase your positivity and confidence."

236
00:13:01.830 --> 00:13:03.840
You can pause to have a think.

237
00:13:03.840 --> 00:13:05.840
Press play when you're ready to move on.

238
00:13:09.000 --> 00:13:11.340
The answer is, Alex.

239
00:13:11.340 --> 00:13:13.170
This was a bit of a tricky question,

240
00:13:13.170 --> 00:13:17.370
because respect for boundaries and kindness

241
00:13:17.370 --> 00:13:20.220
are both important features of friendship.

242
00:13:20.220 --> 00:13:21.810
However, the question was asking

243
00:13:21.810 --> 00:13:24.480
how healthy friendships make people feel,

244
00:13:24.480 --> 00:13:27.720
and Alex talks about positivity and confidence,

245
00:13:27.720 --> 00:13:29.100
which are feelings.

246
00:13:29.100 --> 00:13:30.903
Well done if you got that correct.

247
00:13:33.510 --> 00:13:36.660
That brings us to the first task for today's lesson.

248
00:13:36.660 --> 00:13:37.493
Task A.

249
00:13:38.610 --> 00:13:41.250
Read Isaac's story.

250
00:13:41.250 --> 00:13:44.910
For part one, I'd like you to identify examples

251
00:13:44.910 --> 00:13:47.553
that show the features of a healthy friendship.

252
00:13:48.690 --> 00:13:52.530
For part two, explain how this interaction

253
00:13:52.530 --> 00:13:54.453
might have made Isaac feel.

254
00:13:56.167 --> 00:14:01.167
"Isaac sat at his desk overwhelmed by the pressure of exams.

255
00:14:02.040 --> 00:14:05.103
A message from his friend interrupted his thoughts.

256
00:14:06.060 --> 00:14:08.190
Sensing Isaac's stress,

257
00:14:08.190 --> 00:14:10.950
his friend encouraged him to take a break

258
00:14:10.950 --> 00:14:12.400
and they went through a walk.

259
00:14:13.590 --> 00:14:16.620
After some hesitation, Isaac opened up,

260
00:14:16.620 --> 00:14:18.870
whilst his friend listened carefully

261
00:14:18.870 --> 00:14:21.417
and reminded Isaac of his strengths."

262
00:14:22.470 --> 00:14:25.230
You can pause the video to carry out the task,

263
00:14:25.230 --> 00:14:28.353
and when you're ready to see some answers, just press play.

264
00:14:32.310 --> 00:14:34.623
Let's take a look at the answers together.

265
00:14:36.690 --> 00:14:39.060
You might have said the following.

266
00:14:39.060 --> 00:14:43.080
Number one, Isaac is shown respect by his friend

267
00:14:43.080 --> 00:14:46.230
who listens carefully to his concerns.

268
00:14:46.230 --> 00:14:49.380
He helps him to understand his own boundaries,

269
00:14:49.380 --> 00:14:52.680
encouraging him to take a break from work.

270
00:14:52.680 --> 00:14:54.360
He shows kindness,

271
00:14:54.360 --> 00:14:57.483
walking with Isaac to encourage him to communicate.

272
00:14:58.410 --> 00:15:02.880
Isaac also shows honesty, opening up about his feelings

273
00:15:02.880 --> 00:15:04.953
and showing that he can trust his friend.

274
00:15:07.020 --> 00:15:10.680
For part two, Isaac might have felt a range

275
00:15:10.680 --> 00:15:12.810
of positive feelings.

276
00:15:12.810 --> 00:15:15.810
He would've felt happy to be supported,

277
00:15:15.810 --> 00:15:19.320
safe as a result of having someone to confide in,

278
00:15:19.320 --> 00:15:21.840
as well as more confident in his work

279
00:15:21.840 --> 00:15:24.150
and positive in his outlook.

280
00:15:24.150 --> 00:15:26.013
Well done if you got that correct.

281
00:15:29.640 --> 00:15:32.730
That brings us to the second part of today's lesson,

282
00:15:32.730 --> 00:15:35.553
how can unhealthy friendships make us feel?

283
00:15:38.940 --> 00:15:43.020
Not all friendships are healthy all of the time.

284
00:15:43.020 --> 00:15:45.690
What's important is that we're able to recognise

285
00:15:45.690 --> 00:15:48.093
when a friendship might be unhealthy.

286
00:15:49.500 --> 00:15:52.440
Just like the features of a healthy friendship

287
00:15:52.440 --> 00:15:54.840
that we looked at earlier this lesson,

288
00:15:54.840 --> 00:15:58.140
there are also features of an unhealthy friendship,

289
00:15:58.140 --> 00:16:00.483
and it's important that we know what they are.

290
00:16:01.589 --> 00:16:03.570
A lack of respect.

291
00:16:03.570 --> 00:16:07.320
This is when one friend treats another friend unfairly,

292
00:16:07.320 --> 00:16:08.190
or in a way

293
00:16:08.190 --> 00:16:10.640
that they wouldn't want to be treated themselves.

294
00:16:12.090 --> 00:16:15.000
Not appreciating each other's boundaries.

295
00:16:15.000 --> 00:16:16.260
This could be perhaps

296
00:16:16.260 --> 00:16:18.780
where one friend puts pressure on another

297
00:16:18.780 --> 00:16:21.280
to do something that they're not comfortable with.

298
00:16:22.830 --> 00:16:24.930
A lack of kindness.

299
00:16:24.930 --> 00:16:28.080
This is when a friend doesn't treat another friend

300
00:16:28.080 --> 00:16:31.470
with consideration or thoughtfulness.

301
00:16:31.470 --> 00:16:34.773
It might be unkind words or unkind actions.

302
00:16:36.030 --> 00:16:37.323
A lack of honesty.

303
00:16:38.190 --> 00:16:40.410
In an unhealthy friendship,

304
00:16:40.410 --> 00:16:42.540
people might not feel comfortable enough

305
00:16:42.540 --> 00:16:44.760
to be honest about how they feel.

306
00:16:44.760 --> 00:16:47.163
They might even find they have to hide things.

307
00:16:48.000 --> 00:16:50.700
And, a lack of trust.

308
00:16:50.700 --> 00:16:53.130
This is when a friend can't believe

309
00:16:53.130 --> 00:16:54.990
what another friend is telling them,

310
00:16:54.990 --> 00:16:58.023
and they have doubts about whether they're being honest.

311
00:17:00.210 --> 00:17:02.260
Time for another check for understanding.

312
00:17:03.210 --> 00:17:06.540
Which two features of an unhealthy friendship

313
00:17:06.540 --> 00:17:08.193
are missing from this list?

314
00:17:09.240 --> 00:17:11.220
Lack of kindness,

315
00:17:11.220 --> 00:17:13.110
lack of honesty,

316
00:17:13.110 --> 00:17:15.000
and lack of trust.

317
00:17:15.000 --> 00:17:17.610
You can pause the video to have a quick think.

318
00:17:17.610 --> 00:17:19.860
Just press play when you're ready to move on.

319
00:17:23.490 --> 00:17:26.910
The missing features are lack of respect

320
00:17:26.910 --> 00:17:30.000
and not appreciating each other's boundaries.

321
00:17:30.000 --> 00:17:31.743
Well done if you got that correct.

322
00:17:35.160 --> 00:17:36.810
An unhealthy friendship

323
00:17:36.810 --> 00:17:39.870
is likely to have an impact or an effect

324
00:17:39.870 --> 00:17:41.163
on how we are feeling.

325
00:17:42.150 --> 00:17:44.340
Chloe is sharing a story about a friendship

326
00:17:44.340 --> 00:17:46.170
that is unhealthy.

327
00:17:46.170 --> 00:17:48.330
How might she be feeling?

328
00:17:48.330 --> 00:17:50.640
She says, "I used to feel excited

329
00:17:50.640 --> 00:17:53.742
about hanging out with my best friend since primary school,

330
00:17:53.742 --> 00:17:57.060
but lately, things feel different.

331
00:17:57.060 --> 00:17:58.470
Whenever we are together,

332
00:17:58.470 --> 00:18:01.020
she makes mean jokes about my clothes

333
00:18:01.020 --> 00:18:04.800
or tells secrets I have asked her to keep private."

334
00:18:04.800 --> 00:18:06.810
You can pause the video to have a quick think.

335
00:18:06.810 --> 00:18:09.053
Just press play when you're ready to move on.

336
00:18:12.990 --> 00:18:17.640
The chances are that Chloe feels unsafe, uncomfortable,

337
00:18:17.640 --> 00:18:19.203
and disrespected.

338
00:18:21.900 --> 00:18:23.943
Let's have a look at another scenario.

339
00:18:24.780 --> 00:18:27.270
Jack also shares a story about a friendship

340
00:18:27.270 --> 00:18:29.400
that became unhealthy.

341
00:18:29.400 --> 00:18:31.413
How might he have been feeling?

342
00:18:32.497 --> 00:18:35.730
"I used to really enjoy spending time with my friend,

343
00:18:35.730 --> 00:18:39.600
but more recently, things just haven't felt right.

344
00:18:39.600 --> 00:18:42.300
Every time I don't do what he asks me to,

345
00:18:42.300 --> 00:18:44.490
he calls me boring and laughs at me,

346
00:18:44.490 --> 00:18:48.150
making me feel like I have to do what he wants."

347
00:18:48.150 --> 00:18:50.607
Again, you can pause the video to have a think,

348
00:18:50.607 --> 00:18:53.057
and just press play when you're ready to move on.

349
00:18:56.310 --> 00:18:59.633
The chances are that Jack also feels unsafe,

350
00:18:59.633 --> 00:19:02.640
uncomfortable, and disrespected.

351
00:19:02.640 --> 00:19:04.173
Well done if you got those.

352
00:19:07.530 --> 00:19:11.700
Just like Chloe and Jack, in an unhealthy friendship,

353
00:19:11.700 --> 00:19:13.803
a person might feel unsafe,

354
00:19:15.060 --> 00:19:16.143
uncomfortable,

355
00:19:17.550 --> 00:19:18.633
disrespected.

356
00:19:19.890 --> 00:19:23.670
These feelings can sometimes be difficult to understand

357
00:19:23.670 --> 00:19:25.203
and difficult to manage.

358
00:19:26.340 --> 00:19:28.560
We should always talk to a trusted adult

359
00:19:28.560 --> 00:19:31.053
if we are experiencing these feelings.

360
00:19:33.630 --> 00:19:36.150
Time for another check for understanding.

361
00:19:36.150 --> 00:19:38.700
Which of the following statements best describes

362
00:19:38.700 --> 00:19:42.540
how an unhealthy friendship might make you feel?

363
00:19:42.540 --> 00:19:45.813
A, you might experience a sense of disrespect,

364
00:19:46.770 --> 00:19:49.683
B, there might be a lack of kindness,

365
00:19:50.880 --> 00:19:54.273
and C, you might not know someone's boundaries.

366
00:19:55.230 --> 00:19:56.850
Pause the video to have a think.

367
00:19:56.850 --> 00:19:59.093
Just press play when you're ready to move on.

368
00:20:03.060 --> 00:20:08.060
The answer is A, you might experience a sense of disrespect.

369
00:20:08.340 --> 00:20:10.053
Well done if you got that correct.

370
00:20:13.110 --> 00:20:15.810
That brings us to the second and final task

371
00:20:15.810 --> 00:20:17.220
for today's lesson.

372
00:20:17.220 --> 00:20:18.183
Task B.

373
00:20:19.230 --> 00:20:20.430
Read the scenario

374
00:20:20.430 --> 00:20:22.953
and answer the questions on the next slide.

375
00:20:24.157 --> 00:20:26.370
"We've been friends for years.

376
00:20:26.370 --> 00:20:29.943
She recently spent hours making a card filled with memories.

377
00:20:30.840 --> 00:20:32.100
When I forgot my lunch,

378
00:20:32.100 --> 00:20:34.713
she shared her lunch with me without hesitation.

379
00:20:35.610 --> 00:20:38.370
But our friendship isn't perfect.

380
00:20:38.370 --> 00:20:41.610
She teases me about my clumsiness in front of others,

381
00:20:41.610 --> 00:20:44.523
and though I laugh along, I feel embarrassed.

382
00:20:45.360 --> 00:20:48.540
Recently, when I asked for quiet time to study,

383
00:20:48.540 --> 00:20:50.010
she kept messaging me,

384
00:20:50.010 --> 00:20:53.340
demanding to know why I wasn't replying.

385
00:20:53.340 --> 00:20:57.150
Once she shared a secret I had trusted her with at school,

386
00:20:57.150 --> 00:20:59.553
brushing it off as not a big deal.

387
00:21:00.480 --> 00:21:02.700
Though we care deeply for each other,

388
00:21:02.700 --> 00:21:05.937
we both realised our friendship needed to change."

389
00:21:08.040 --> 00:21:09.360
The questions are,

390
00:21:09.360 --> 00:21:13.890
number one, identify three statements from the scenario

391
00:21:13.890 --> 00:21:16.500
that exemplify, that means show,

392
00:21:16.500 --> 00:21:18.543
the features of a healthy friendship.

393
00:21:19.770 --> 00:21:23.730
Number two, identify three statements from the scenario

394
00:21:23.730 --> 00:21:25.740
that exemplify or show

395
00:21:25.740 --> 00:21:27.903
the features of an unhealthy friendship.

396
00:21:29.040 --> 00:21:33.540
And number three, explain how the person in the scenario

397
00:21:33.540 --> 00:21:36.300
might be feeling as a result of the friendship

398
00:21:36.300 --> 00:21:37.173
that they are in.

399
00:21:38.250 --> 00:21:40.620
You can pause the video to do this task.

400
00:21:40.620 --> 00:21:43.320
When you're ready to see the answers, just press play.

401
00:21:47.100 --> 00:21:48.123
How did you get on?

402
00:21:48.960 --> 00:21:51.310
Let's have a look at possible answers together.

403
00:21:54.155 --> 00:21:55.320
Your answers to the questions

404
00:21:55.320 --> 00:21:57.540
might have included the following.

405
00:21:57.540 --> 00:22:00.270
Number one, "She recently spent hours

406
00:22:00.270 --> 00:22:02.430
making a card filled with memories."

407
00:22:02.430 --> 00:22:04.203
This shows kindness.

408
00:22:05.610 --> 00:22:06.487
Number two,

409
00:22:06.487 --> 00:22:09.660
"She shared her lunch with me without hesitation."

410
00:22:09.660 --> 00:22:12.273
This shows kindness and respect.

411
00:22:13.127 --> 00:22:14.587
And number three,

412
00:22:14.587 --> 00:22:17.880
"We both realised our friendship needed to change."

413
00:22:17.880 --> 00:22:19.533
This shows honesty.

414
00:22:22.470 --> 00:22:24.667
For question number two.

415
00:22:24.667 --> 00:22:27.630
"She teases me about my clumsiness."

416
00:22:27.630 --> 00:22:31.833
This shows a lack of respect and a lack of kindness.

417
00:22:32.947 --> 00:22:34.560
"She kept messaging me,

418
00:22:34.560 --> 00:22:37.290
demanding to know why I wasn't replying."

419
00:22:37.290 --> 00:22:39.843
This is not appreciating boundaries.

420
00:22:41.100 --> 00:22:43.260
And, "Once she shared a secret

421
00:22:43.260 --> 00:22:45.540
that I'd trusted her with at school."

422
00:22:45.540 --> 00:22:48.453
This shows a lack of trust and a lack of honesty.

423
00:22:51.360 --> 00:22:52.923
And finally, number three.

424
00:22:54.420 --> 00:22:57.540
The person might be feeling really conflicted,

425
00:22:57.540 --> 00:22:58.740
because there are features

426
00:22:58.740 --> 00:23:01.833
of both a healthy and unhealthy friendship.

427
00:23:03.090 --> 00:23:05.250
They might also be feeling glad

428
00:23:05.250 --> 00:23:07.830
that they have both acknowledged this issue

429
00:23:07.830 --> 00:23:09.960
and agree that things need to change

430
00:23:09.960 --> 00:23:12.630
in order for them to have a more healthy relationship

431
00:23:12.630 --> 00:23:14.490
moving forward.

432
00:23:14.490 --> 00:23:17.373
Well done if your answers were along those lines.

433
00:23:23.370 --> 00:23:26.460
You've reached the end of today's lesson.

434
00:23:26.460 --> 00:23:27.600
Before we finish,

435
00:23:27.600 --> 00:23:30.393
let's take a quick look at today's lesson summary.

436
00:23:31.890 --> 00:23:35.673
Friendships can exist in person and online.

437
00:23:37.020 --> 00:23:41.550
Healthy friendships can make us feel happy, confident,

438
00:23:41.550 --> 00:23:43.743
safe, and positive.

439
00:23:45.450 --> 00:23:47.340
People have boundaries,

440
00:23:47.340 --> 00:23:50.493
and these should be respected in healthy friendships.

441
00:23:52.320 --> 00:23:56.040
Unhealthy friendships can make us feel unsafe,

442
00:23:56.040 --> 00:23:58.953
uncomfortable, or disrespected.

443
00:24:00.240 --> 00:24:03.060
If we feel this way in a friendship,

444
00:24:03.060 --> 00:24:05.103
we should speak to a trusted adult.

445
00:24:06.682 --> 00:24:09.630
Friendships evolve over time

446
00:24:09.630 --> 00:24:12.480
and do not always neatly fit into the categories

447
00:24:12.480 --> 00:24:14.283
healthy and unhealthy.

448
00:24:16.050 --> 00:24:18.810
Well done on all your hard work today.

449
00:24:18.810 --> 00:24:21.000
I hope that you've got a better understanding

450
00:24:21.000 --> 00:24:22.750
of what makes a healthy friendship.

451
00:24:25.920 --> 00:24:28.530
If you need further support or guidance

452
00:24:28.530 --> 00:24:30.900
on anything that you've learned about today,

453
00:24:30.900 --> 00:24:32.763
please speak to your trusted adult.

454
00:24:34.050 --> 00:24:36.060
Together with your trusted adult,

455
00:24:36.060 --> 00:24:38.040
you can also find more information

456
00:24:38.040 --> 00:24:40.050
at the following websites.

457
00:24:40.050 --> 00:24:43.170
Childline, a website and phone line

458
00:24:43.170 --> 00:24:46.233
which is able to offer confidential advice and support.

459
00:24:47.310 --> 00:24:48.300
And CEOP.

460
00:24:49.950 --> 00:24:51.690
CEOP helps protect children

461
00:24:51.690 --> 00:24:54.333
from online abuse and exploitation.

lessons.unitTitle: Healthy relationships: How can I build good relationships?

lessonKeywords.description: a relationship between two or more people who care about and support each other
being aware of the dangers or threats you could encounter when online
the exchange of words, either verbal or written, to express thoughts, feelings and ideas

keyLearningPoints.keyLearningPoint: There are signs of healthy friendships.
There are different ways to make new freinds.
It can be unsafe to make new friends online.

misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.response: You don't have to spend lots of time with people for them to be good friends.
misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.misconception: I can only be friends with someone I see a lot.

lessons.pupilLessonOutcome: I can explain how I can make new friends safely.

teacherTips.teacherTip: Adapt this lesson by adding in the details of all the clubs and activities at your school and in your local area.

lessons.transcript_sentences:
Hello, my name is Ms. Wittams-Howarth.
Welcome to today's lesson on making new friends.

lessons.unitTitle: Healthy relationships: How can I build good relationships?

lessonKeywords.description: a close relationship between two or more people who care about and support each other
a disagreement between two or more people
the ability to manage your emotions, and think rationally even if you are upset or angry

keyLearningPoints.keyLearningPoint: Children change as they grow and develop, this means friendships can change too.
Not all friendships are 'forever'.
It is important to speak to our friends, family or teachers if we are concerned about a friendship.

misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.response: It is natural for people to drift apart and discover different interests or hobbies, particularly as they grow older. It it important to remember that friendships don't last forever, and this is ok, you will experience other friendships in your life.
misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.misconception: If a friend falls out with me or we start to grow apart, I should do whatever it takes to make them my friend again.

lessons.pupilLessonOutcome: I can explain why and how friendships change and how I can support myself.

teacherTips.teacherTip: Discuss with the class who they can turn to for pastoral support in your setting.

lessons.unitTitle: Healthy relationships: How do relationships change?

lessonKeywords.description: when a couple live together without being married or in a civil partnership

keyLearningPoints.keyLearningPoint: There are different types of long-term relationships including marriage, civil partnerships and cohabitation.
A person should only enter a long-term relationship when they feel emotionally ready and there is no pressure.
All healthy long-term relationships are based on mutual respect and consent.
People may choose to enter the different types of long-term relationships for different reasons.
Cohabitation involves living together without being married or in a civil partnership.

misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.response: Cohabitation does not provide the same legal rights and responsibilities as marriage or civil partnerships. It's important to understand these differences.
misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.misconception: Cohabitation provides people with the same legal rights and responsibilities as being married.

teacherTips.teacherTip: Reinforce that all choices of long-term relationships are valid if they are freely entered into.

Family circumstances.

There are different types of long-term relationships,

keyLearningPoints.keyLearningPoint: Civil partnership is a legally recognised union with rights similar to marriage.
People might choose civil partnership for legal, personal or financial reasons.
The Civil Partnership Act 2004 is the key legislation governing civil partnerships in the UK.
Civil partnerships are available to both same-sex and opposite-sex couples.
Civil partnerships offer similar legal protections as marriage.

misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.response: Since 2019, civil partnerships have been available to both same-sex and opposite-sex couples in the UK.
misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.misconception: Civil partnership is only for same-sex couples.

00:19:37.290 --> 00:19:39.600
the key learning from today's lesson.

455
00:19:39.600 --> 00:19:41.040
In today's lesson we've learned

456
00:19:41.040 --> 00:19:43.860
that a civil partnership is a legally recognized union

457
00:19:43.860 --> 00:19:46.080
with similar rights to marriage.

458
00:19:46.080 --> 00:19:48.120
The Civil Partnership Act 2004

459
00:19:48.120 --> 00:19:51.600
is the law that governs civil partnerships in the UK,

460
00:19:51.600 --> 00:19:53.220
and since 2019,

461
00:19:53.220 --> 00:19:54.870
civil partnerships are available

462
00:19:54.870 --> 00:19:58.680
to both same-sex and opposite-sex couples in the UK.

463
00:19:58.680 --> 00:20:00.570
People may choose civil partnership

464
00:20:00.570 --> 00:20:03.660
for legal, personal, or financial reasons.

465
00:20:03.660 --> 00:20:06.240
For instance, a civil partnership grants couples

466
00:20:06.240 --> 00:20:08.550
legal rights that they would not otherwise have

467
00:20:08.550 --> 00:20:09.990
if they were just cohabiting,

468
00:20:09.990 --> 00:20:11.850
which means living together.

469

And a civil partnership can end through dissolution,

470
00:20:14.400 --> 00:20:16.443
which is a process similar to divorce.

lessons.unitTitle: Healthy relationships: How do relationships change?

lessonKeywords.description: being considerate of others and the world around you; treating people fairly and how you would like to be treated
the confidence that someone will act in your best interest and be honest with you
the exchange of words, either verbal or written, to express thoughts, feelings and ideas
an imaginary line separating what we will and won't allow
in this context, something shared between partners in a fair and equal way, such as respect or trust

keyLearningPoints.keyLearningPoint: A healthy romantic relationship is based on mutual respect and trust.
Communication is key to maintaining a healthy romantic relationship.
Boundaries are important in a romantic relationship to ensure mutual respect.
Trust is built over time through consistent and honest behaviour.

misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.response: Boundaries should be mutually respected. If our boundaries do not align with another person's, or they do not respect our boundaries, then a relationship is not healthy.
misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.misconception: We should alter our boundaries to suit what our partner wants and expects.

keyLearningPoints.keyLearningPoint: Marriage is a legally or formally recognised union of two people as partners in a personal relationship.
People choose to marry for various reasons including love, commitment and legal benefits.
Marriage laws in the UK provide legal protections and rights to married couples.

misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.response: While love and commitment are central to marriage, it also involves legal rights and responsibilities that have financial and social implications.
misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.misconception: Marriage is only about love.

lessons.unitTitle: Our online lives: How can I stay in control online?

lessonKeywords.description: a large official organisation, such as a college, university or hospital
a person or organisation that hires and pays people to work for them
someone who witnesses something

keyLearningPoints.keyLearningPoint: We have a lot of power in the online space to keep ourselves safe.
Institutions might use our social media to find out more about us.
We can use settings and online tools to control what we see and who can contact us.
We can be positive and active bystanders to online abuse.
Negative actions online can have a huge impact on others.

misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.response: What you post online can affect others — it might hurt someone, spread misinformation, or damage your reputation. Once it’s out there, you can’t always take it back.
misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.misconception: What I post online is my business, it doesn't impact anyone else.

lessons.pupilLessonOutcome: I can describe the ways in which I have power online and explain how to use my power online responsibly.

teacherTips.teacherTip: Show some anonymised social media posts (some positive and some ambiguous / some negative)  and evaluate what potential employers might think about the person posting / sharing them.

contentGuidance.contentGuidanceLabel: Depiction or discussion of discriminatory behaviour
contentGuidance.contentGuidanceDescription: Discriminatory behaviour or images, whether on the grounds of race, gender, disability, religion or belief or sexual orientation, or otherwise.

contentGuidance.contentGuidanceLabel: Depiction or discussion of peer pressure or bullying
contentGuidance.contentGuidanceDescription: Depiction or discussion of distress or humiliation e.g. bullying.

lessons.transcript_sentences:
Hi, I'm Ms. Lowe, and I'm your RSHE teacher for today.
Thank you so much for choosing to complete your learning with me.
Now, today's lesson is all about using my personal power online, and because of some of the themes and the topics that we're gonna cover together today, it's important that you complete your learning with the company of an adult.
By the end of today's lesson, you're going to be able to describe the ways in which I have power online, and you're gonna be able to explain how to use your power online responsibly.
Every RSHE lesson should begin with a set of ground rules.
This ensures that every conversation had in RSHE is respectful and we're all able to learn effectively.
So Laura is reminding us that in RSHE, we should listen to others.
It's okay to disagree with each other, but we should listen properly before making assumptions or deciding how to respond.
And when disagreeing, we challenge the statement and not the person.
Andeep is reminding us to respect privacy.
We can discuss examples, but we don't use names or descriptions that can identify anyone, including ourselves.
Izzy is reminding us to choose a level of participation that suits us.
Everyone has the right to choose not to answer a question or to join in a discussion, but we never put anyone on the spot.
And finally, Jacob is reminding us that in RSHE, there is no judgement.
We can explore beliefs and misunderstandings about a topic without the fear of being judged.
Let's have a look at our keywords for today's lesson.
Institution: a large official organisation such as a college, university, or hospital.
Employer: a person or organisation that hires and pays people to work for them.
Bystander: someone who witnesses something.
So here's an outline of what we're gonna be learning together today, and we're gonna begin by asking the question, what power do we have online? So although the internet can feel overwhelming and incredibly vast, we as individuals do have power online.
We have the power to shape the way that the internet behaves for us, and this can be invaluable in helping our online lives be enjoyable, but also safe.
One of the powers that we have online is to make our voices heard.
Due to social media, online community messaging boards, and video sites, we are able to express our thoughts and opinions to millions of people across the globe.
As long as our voices are promoting helpful, positive, or inspiring messages, this can be a real power for good.
We also have the power, sorry, to influence other people.
Aisha is telling us here that this power comes with the responsibility to make sure our influence online is a positive one.
You don't have to have millions of followers in order to exercise power online.
Even if you only have a few followers or a few friends online, the things that you say and the things that you do will inevitably influence other people.
The things that we like, that we share and promote to the people in our online spaces can help to shape their ideas and opinions too.
Now, we're gonna pause here and we're gonna check our understanding.
True or false: the internet is too big a space for us to have any power online? I want you to pause the video here and have a think about your answer.
Really well done if you said false, but why is this false? Well, we have the power to shape the internet in a way that suits us.
This can make the internet a more safe and enjoyable place to be.
We also have the power of information.
I want you to think of the internet as like a giant library that contains a vast collection of human knowledge from all across the globe.
And I think often, this power is one that we take for granted because never before in human history have we had access to so much information at our fingertips.
We also have the power to share this information with others.
Another power that we have is the power to shape how other people see us.
Our online lives, the things that we post, that we share, that we create are visible to lots of different people, places, and institutions.
These things that we post, share, and do online can change the way that other people perceive us.
This is a really powerful tool because the things that we do online can either make a positive or a negative impression on the people who do see us online.
Another power that we have is the power to keep ourselves safe online.
We have privacy and security settings on all the sites and the apps that we use that can help to keep us safe from harm online.
We have the power to choose who can see what we post, who can interact with us, and the content that we see, important power that we have online.
We also have the power to find meaningful and enjoyable work online.
There are sites dedicated to job searching.
There are message boards where employers can post opportunities and allow us to find jobs that suit us.
This can help us to build a better life offline, so again, a really important power.
Now, we're gonna pause here and we're gonna check our understanding.
What word is missing from the sentence? We have the power online to keep ourselves.
Pause the video here and try and fill in that missing word.
Really well done if you said safe.
Yeah, all the sites and the apps that we use every day have security settings that we can use in order to keep ourselves safe and make our online experiences enjoyable.
And now, we're gonna put all the excellent learning into practise.
So around this image of the smartphone, I'd like you to label four to five powers that we have online.
You're gonna pause the video here and write down your answers.
So you were asked to label this image with four or five powers that we have online, and in your answers, you might have said that we have the power to influence other people, the power to make our voices heard, the power to find meaningful and fulfilling employment, the power to keep ourselves safe, and the power of information.
Well done if you mentioned any of those things in your answer.
We're moving on now to the second part of our lesson, where we're asking the question, how can we use this power that we have online responsibly? So as the famous saying goes, "With great power comes great responsibility," and this is no different online.
All those powers that we just had a look at then, we have to use responsibly because those powers have the ability to make a positive and helpful impact on other people if we use them responsibly.
Andeep is telling us here that, on the other hand, when we use our power online irresponsibly, we have a huge negative impact on others and ourselves.
We have the power online to influence others in many different ways.
Now, in order to use this power responsibly, we should be conscious of the content that we share and promote to others.
We should be authentic to ourselves online and communicate with others in a constructive way.
Aisha's telling us here that she shares information on causes that really matter to her.
"By sharing educational content about these things, I can influence others to learn more about the world around them and become better advocates for their own causes." So we can see here that Aisha is using that power of influence in a really constructive and positive way.
Using our powers responsibly online means being aware of how the things that we post affect the way that institutions and employers view us.
Our social media posts can be visible to anyone who searches for them.
I want you to imagine your social media profile as like an additional CV, representing who you are outside of work.
If we're responsible online with our posts, what we're gonna do is create a really positive image for those institutions and employers who look for us.
David is telling us here that he knows that, depending on what he shares online, an employer could make a negative assumption about him.
Now, we're gonna pause here and we're gonna check our understanding.
True or false: our social media profiles are ours to post whatever we want? It doesn't matter what other people think.
Is that true or false? Pause the video here.
Really well done if you said false, but why is this false? Well, our social media can be looked at by employers and institutions, and it can either present you positively or negatively depending on the content that you post, share, and interact with.
If you remember, we said that we should think of our social media profiles as like an additional CV that an employer is gonna have a look at, and it represents what we are like outside of work.
So there are way, sorry, to ensure that employers and institutions can see us in a positive light if they search for us online.
So one of the things that we can do is to decide what we keep public and private online.
We should be sensible about what we share.
That means not sharing any harmful or negative content online.
And we should have a think about how we want other people to see us.
For example, if we post about our hobbies or sporting achievements, we can appear to others as motivated and hardworking.
Now, our voices that we have online can be really powerful forces.
People who aren't responsible with their voices online can cause harm to others, not only online, but in real life as well.
Some people may use their voice online to spread disinformation.
This is purposefully spreading misleading, false, or inaccurate information to others.
They may use their voices online to discriminate against other people.
They may use it to bully and troll others, harm others, and more.
The voices that we use online can have an impact on how others not only see us, but also themselves.
Now, we're gonna pause here and we're gonna check our understanding.
So what I'd like for you to do is rewrite the following sentence to make the statement correct.
So it currently says, "We don't have responsibility online and our online voices cannot harm or impact anyone in real life." I want you to pause the video here and rewrite that sentence.
Great work.
So what you might have written is that, "We have responsibility online because our voices can harm or impact other people in real life." Well done if you rewrote that sentence in that way.
So another way that we can use our power online responsibly and positively is by not being a bystander.
Now, if you're not sure what a bystander is, it is somebody who has seen or witnessed a harmful event.
That could be online or in person.
There are also different types of bystanders.
So Lucas is telling us here that when somebody witnesses bullying or harmful behaviour online and does nothing, this is called being a passive bystander.
If we witness online bullying or harmful behaviour online, ignoring it is an irresponsible use of our online voices.
So what we can do is we can utilise those powers given to us through social media sites and the settings that we have on these apps and websites in order to avoid being a passive bystander.
To be responsible, we should report accounts that are involved in any harmful behaviour online, we should block the accounts that we don't want to see or interact with, we should check in with others online if they're experiencing cyberbullying, and we should tell a trusted adult.
Now, if somebody were to do any of those things when they witness harmful behaviour, they become an active bystander.
Now, we're gonna pause here and we're gonna put our learning into action.
So which of the following is an example of using our power online responsibly? We have blocking and reporting harmful counts, being a passive bystander when we witness harmful behaviour, reaching out to a victim of cyberbullying, and telling a trusted adult about the cyberbullying.
So pause the video here and have a think about your answers.
Really well done if you said B, being a passive bystander when we witness harmful behaviour is using our power online irresponsibly.
Now, we're gonna put our learning into practise, so what I want for you to do is explain in one paragraph what powers we have online and how we can use them responsibly.
So in your answer, I want you to consider the following: the way employers and institutions sees us; settings and security; and being a bystander.
So I need to pause video here and write down those answers.
Excellent work.
So you were asked to explain in one paragraph what powers we have online and how we can use them responsibly.
And in your answers, you might have mentioned the following: "We have significant power online to shape our internet experience and influence others.
Our digital voices can have a positive impact, but we must use this power responsibly.
Sharing harmful content or disinformation can lead employers and institutions to make negative judgements about us, as our social media profiles can function as an additional CV, representing our character outside of work.
Through security settings, we can control what content we see, who interacts with us, and what we keep private.
When we witness harmful behaviour online, we shouldn't remain passive bystanders.
Instead, we should take action by reporting and blocking accounts, telling a trusted adult, and reaching out to the victims. Using our power online responsibly means staying authentic to ourselves while communicating with others in a constructive way." Now, let's go through a summary of what we've learned together today.
Despite the vast size of the internet, we have power online to keep ourselves and others safe.
The things we post on social media can be visible to institutions and employers, and they may use this as a way to learn more about our lives offline.
We have the power to control what others see of us and what we see from others using the settings and security tools available to us online.
Our actions can affect others in real life.
If we witness harmful behaviour online, we should be responsible and not be passive bystanders.
To avoid being a passive bystander, we should block and report harmful accounts, tell a trusted adult, and reach out to the victims of cyberbullying.
If any of the things that we've covered together in today's lesson affect you in any way or you have any concerns, here are some places you can go to to access support.
First, we have Childline, a website and phone line which is able to offer confidential advice and support, CEOP, which helps protect children from online abuse and exploitation, and finally, Internet Matters, which teaches children and parents how to stay safe and happy online while using the internet.
And I would like to say a huge well done for all of your fantastic work that we've done together today.
It's been a pleasure to teach you, and I look forward to seeing you in another RSHE lesson soon.

keyLearningPoints.keyLearningPoint: A secure website uses HTTPS and has a padlock symbol in the address bar.
Common online financial risks include phishing, identity theft and fake websites.
Strategies to avoid scams include: strong passwords, enabling multi-factor authentication and being cautious of emails.
Online scams can be very sophisticated and can be hard to spot.
Phishing and fake sites can be used to steal passwords.

We are more susceptible to financial security risks if we use public WiFi networks when accessing banking sites or inputting sensitive data.
Public WiFi networks do not always have a high level of security and, therefore, can be open to the "man in the middle" attacks.
"Man in the middle" attacks occur when a cyber attacker hacks into a network and places themselves between the user and the website they're connecting to.
The process works like this.
The user accesses their banking site on an unsecure WiFi network.
The hacker intercepts the data and passwords as the user enters them.

If you are unsure, contact the real company to confirm whether it was them or not.

00:09:27.300 --> 00:09:31.020
Furthermore, those who experience harassment online

153
00:09:31.020 --> 00:09:33.423
may develop mental health conditions.

154
00:09:35.910 --> 00:09:37.713
Okay, time for a task now.

155
00:09:38.550 --> 00:09:40.110
Answer the question.

156
00:09:40.110 --> 00:09:43.320
Is everyone equally vulnerable online?

157
00:09:43.320 --> 00:09:46.653
Now, you must answer this question in a full paragraph.

158
00:09:47.640 --> 00:09:50.700
Pause this video so you can have some time to do the task,

159
00:09:50.700 --> 00:09:53.100
and then we can go through the answers together.

160
00:10:01.950 --> 00:10:04.620
Okay, well done for having a go.

161
00:10:04.620 --> 00:10:07.803
In your paragraph, you might have included the following.

162
00:10:08.797 --> 00:10:11.880
"Although anyone can face online harassment,

163
00:10:11.880 --> 00:10:15.960
some people are more likely to experience it than others.

164
00:10:15.960 --> 00:10:20.940
For example, girls and women, members of the LGBT community,

165
00:10:20.940 --> 00:10:23.013
and people with disabilities.

166
00:10:23.850 --> 00:10:26.610
This harassment is often aimed at someone

167
00:10:26.610 --> 00:10:29.370
because of their protected characteristic,

168
00:10:29.370 --> 00:10:33.570
which can make them feel unwelcome in online spaces.

169
00:10:33.570 --> 00:10:37.410
Some online harassment may be considered hate speech,

170
00:10:37.410 --> 00:10:40.740
which includes threats against individuals or groups

171
00:10:40.740 --> 00:10:43.740
and spreading harmful stereotypes.

172
00:10:43.740 --> 00:10:48.740
Hate speech and harassment are unacceptable in any context.

173
00:10:49.320 --> 00:10:51.690
They can have serious consequences

174
00:10:51.690 --> 00:10:54.780
'cause they may incite people to real-world violence

175
00:10:54.780 --> 00:10:57.840
against particular individuals or groups

176
00:10:57.840 --> 00:11:01.110
and victims may develop mental health conditions

177
00:11:01.110 --> 00:11:02.307
as a result."

178
00:11:03.840 --> 00:11:06.183
Well done if your answer was similar to mine.

179
00:11:08.899 --> 00:11:10.830
We're now going to move on to the second

180
00:11:10.830 --> 00:11:13.290
and the final part of our lesson,

181
00:11:13.290 --> 00:11:16.743
What can I do about online harassment?

182
00:11:18.990 --> 00:11:21.090
We all have a role to play

183
00:11:21.090 --> 00:11:25.410
in creating safer, more inclusive online spaces

184
00:11:25.410 --> 00:11:27.150
that reduce the harms

185
00:11:27.150 --> 00:11:30.390
of online harassment and hate speech.

186
00:11:30.390 --> 00:11:33.783
Small actions can make a big difference.

187
00:11:35.370 --> 00:11:38.610
Police Officer Paula says, "If everyone stands up

188
00:11:38.610 --> 00:11:41.280
to online harassment and hate speech,

189
00:11:41.280 --> 00:11:43.227
we can make the internet a safer

190
00:11:43.227 --> 00:11:45.213
and more welcoming space for all.

191
00:11:48.814 --> 00:11:50.040
Here are some ways

192
00:11:50.040 --> 00:11:52.983
that you can be a positive digital citizen.

193
00:11:54.180 --> 00:11:57.390
Report online harassment and hate speech.

194
00:11:57.390 --> 00:12:00.693
Use the platform's built-in tools to do this.

195
00:12:01.740 --> 00:12:04.800
Support victims if you know them in person,

196
00:12:04.800 --> 00:12:06.480
so you might do this by sending them

197
00:12:06.480 --> 00:12:08.583
a private message of support.

198
00:12:09.780 --> 00:12:12.270
Think before you post.

199
00:12:12.270 --> 00:12:15.783
Consider how your words might affect others.

200
00:12:17.190 --> 00:12:19.740
Amplify positive voices.

201
00:12:19.740 --> 00:12:24.603
Like, share, and comment on content that spreads kindness.

202
00:12:26.100 --> 00:12:28.380
Use inclusive language.

203
00:12:28.380 --> 00:12:30.930
That means avoiding words and phrases

204
00:12:30.930 --> 00:12:33.603
that might exclude or hurt others.

205
00:12:35.040 --> 00:12:36.870
Respect privacy.

206
00:12:36.870 --> 00:12:40.290
Do not share photos or information about others

207
00:12:40.290 --> 00:12:41.553
without their permission.

208
00:12:42.510 --> 00:12:44.130
And be authentic.

209
00:12:44.130 --> 00:12:46.713
Don't pretend to be someone you're not online.

210
00:12:49.890 --> 00:12:53.190
How do I support someone experiencing harassment?

211
00:12:53.190 --> 00:12:56.370
Well, you should listen without judgement .

212
00:12:56.370 --> 00:13:00.150
Let them know you believe them and it's not their fault.

213
00:13:00.150 --> 00:13:02.460
Encourage them to report.

214
00:13:02.460 --> 00:13:06.150
Offer to help them report the harassment to the platform.

215
00:13:06.150 --> 00:13:08.250
Help them save the evidence.

216
00:13:08.250 --> 00:13:11.250
Screenshots can be important for reports.

217
00:13:11.250 --> 00:13:13.050
And stay connected.

218
00:13:13.050 --> 00:13:15.723
Check in with them regularly to show that you care.

219
00:13:18.000 --> 00:13:20.190
An active bystander works

220
00:13:20.190 --> 00:13:24.060
to stop harassment rather than just watching it happen

221
00:13:24.060 --> 00:13:27.693
and aims to contribute to positive online spaces.

222
00:13:29.340 --> 00:13:32.220
Here are some ways that you can do this.

223
00:13:32.220 --> 00:13:33.930
Standing up against harassment

224
00:13:33.930 --> 00:13:36.930
when you see it in a safe way,

225
00:13:36.930 --> 00:13:40.860
celebrating others' achievements and milestones,

226
00:13:40.860 --> 00:13:45.540
sharing educational content that helps others to learn,

227
00:13:45.540 --> 00:13:49.113
and modelling the behaviour you want to see from others.

228
00:13:51.720 --> 00:13:54.450
Police Officer Paula says, "Remember,

229
00:13:54.450 --> 00:13:57.840
the internet reflects the people who use it.

230
00:13:57.840 --> 00:14:02.250
By choosing to be kind, respectful, and supportive online,

231
00:14:02.250 --> 00:14:04.980
you're helping to create the kind of digital world

232
00:14:04.980 --> 00:14:06.387
you want to be a part of."

233
00:14:09.540 --> 00:14:12.420
Okay, time for a check for understanding.

234
00:14:12.420 --> 00:14:16.950
Who has responsibility to stand up to online harassment?

235
00:14:16.950 --> 00:14:19.500
Is it A, only adults,

236
00:14:19.500 --> 00:14:23.160
B, site administrators and moderators,

237
00:14:23.160 --> 00:14:25.620
or C, everyone?

238
00:14:25.620 --> 00:14:27.360
Pause this video so you can have some time

239
00:14:27.360 --> 00:14:28.923
to think about your answer.

240
00:14:35.760 --> 00:14:38.280
Okay, well done if you said C,

241
00:14:38.280 --> 00:14:40.890
everyone has the responsibility to stand up

242
00:14:40.890 --> 00:14:42.810
to online harassment.

243
00:14:42.810 --> 00:14:45.630
Okay, let's do another check for understanding.

244
00:14:45.630 --> 00:14:47.070
List three to four ways

245
00:14:47.070 --> 00:14:50.520
that you can be a positive digital citizen.

246
00:14:50.520 --> 00:14:53.133
Pause this video so you can think about your answer.

247
00:15:02.220 --> 00:15:04.230
Okay, so you might have said,

248
00:15:04.230 --> 00:15:07.320
reporting online harassment and hate speech,

249
00:15:07.320 --> 00:15:11.160
supporting victims of online harassment and hate speech,

250
00:15:11.160 --> 00:15:13.200
thinking before you post,

251
00:15:13.200 --> 00:15:17.940
amplifying positive voices, using inclusive language,

252
00:15:17.940 --> 00:15:21.420
respecting privacy, and being authentic.

253
00:15:21.420 --> 00:15:23.670
Well done if your answer was similar to mine.

254
00:15:25.950 --> 00:15:29.550
Social media and community platforms have settings

255
00:15:29.550 --> 00:15:34.110
that can enable us to take action against online harassment.

256
00:15:34.110 --> 00:15:36.570
For example, settings that allow us

257
00:15:36.570 --> 00:15:40.353
to block, mute, and report other users.

258
00:15:42.030 --> 00:15:45.030
If we witness or experience harassment online,

259
00:15:45.030 --> 00:15:49.410
we should report the account responsible,

260
00:15:49.410 --> 00:15:51.510
block the account,

261
00:15:51.510 --> 00:15:56.010
tell a trusted adult about what we have seen or experienced,

262
00:15:56.010 --> 00:15:59.250
and reach out to the person experiencing harassment

263
00:15:59.250 --> 00:16:00.933
and offer them support.

264
00:16:02.700 --> 00:16:05.013
We should never retaliate against people

265
00:16:05.013 --> 00:16:07.980
that are harassing others online.

266
00:16:07.980 --> 00:16:11.463
This includes sending comments or messages back to the user.

267
00:16:13.230 --> 00:16:16.890
Police Officer Paula says, "Retaliating against people

268
00:16:16.890 --> 00:16:19.890
who are engaging in harmful behaviour online

269
00:16:19.890 --> 00:16:23.787
can escalate things and make the situation worse."

270
00:16:26.160 --> 00:16:28.590
Okay, time for a check for understanding.

271
00:16:28.590 --> 00:16:31.140
Change one word in this sentence

272
00:16:31.140 --> 00:16:33.607
to make the statement correct.

273
00:16:33.607 --> 00:16:36.270
"We should always retaliate against people

274
00:16:36.270 --> 00:16:38.397
that are harassing others online."

275
00:16:39.390 --> 00:16:41.760
Okay, so which word are you going to change

276
00:16:41.760 --> 00:16:44.280
to make that statement correct?

277
00:16:44.280 --> 00:16:46.953
Pause this video so you can have some thinking time.

278
00:16:57.420 --> 00:17:01.200
Okay, well done if you change the word always to never.

279
00:17:01.200 --> 00:17:03.930
We should never retaliate against people

280
00:17:03.930 --> 00:17:06.303
that are harassing others online.

281
00:17:09.000 --> 00:17:11.640
Online harassment can be unlawful

282
00:17:11.640 --> 00:17:15.630
if it meets one or more of the following conditions.

283
00:17:15.630 --> 00:17:20.130
It causes fear or violence, so physical safety concerns,

284
00:17:20.130 --> 00:17:22.860
it causes alarm or distress,

285
00:17:22.860 --> 00:17:26.220
it involves threats or abusive messages,

286
00:17:26.220 --> 00:17:28.710
or if it involves repeated conduct

287
00:17:28.710 --> 00:17:30.843
on at least two occasions.

288
00:17:32.580 --> 00:17:34.717
Police Officer Paula States,

289
00:17:34.717 --> 00:17:37.890
"Although there is no exact legal definition

290
00:17:37.890 --> 00:17:40.350
of online bullying and harassment,

291
00:17:40.350 --> 00:17:44.310
it can be prosecuted under a number of UK laws,

292
00:17:44.310 --> 00:17:48.270
including the Malicious Communications Act,

293
00:17:48.270 --> 00:17:51.600
Criminal Justice and Public Order Act,

294
00:17:51.600 --> 00:17:54.270
Protection from Harassment Act,

295
00:17:54.270 --> 00:17:57.780
Communications Act, Defamation Act,

296
00:17:57.780 --> 00:17:59.793
and Online Safety Act.

297
00:18:02.640 --> 00:18:04.590
Police Officer Paula also states

298
00:18:04.590 --> 00:18:06.990
that being found guilty of an offence

299
00:18:06.990 --> 00:18:11.040
relating to online harassment under any of these laws

300
00:18:11.040 --> 00:18:15.330
could result in a fine or a prison sentence.

301
00:18:15.330 --> 00:18:16.920
It is a serious offence

302
00:18:16.920 --> 00:18:20.100
to make another person concerned for their safety

303
00:18:20.100 --> 00:18:22.803
through cyber bullying or harassment.

304
00:18:25.140 --> 00:18:28.416
Police Officer Paula states, "To report online harassment

305
00:18:28.416 --> 00:18:32.280
or hate speech, You can also contact the police

306
00:18:32.280 --> 00:18:34.657
on the non-emergency number 101.

307
00:18:38.190 --> 00:18:39.967
Police Officer Paula states,

308
00:18:39.967 --> 00:18:43.950
"Online hate speech can be considered unlawful behaviour

309
00:18:43.950 --> 00:18:46.650
if the intention behind a person's words

310
00:18:46.650 --> 00:18:50.220
is to stir up hatred towards or violence against

311
00:18:50.220 --> 00:18:51.933
an individual or group.

312
00:18:53.400 --> 00:18:56.970
Being found guilty of an offence relating to hate speech

313
00:18:56.970 --> 00:18:59.493
can result in a prison sentence.

314
00:19:01.260 --> 00:19:03.600
Okay, time for a check for understanding.

315
00:19:03.600 --> 00:19:04.980
True or false?

316
00:19:04.980 --> 00:19:08.493
There are no consequences for online harassment.

317
00:19:09.360 --> 00:19:11.070
Pause this video so you can have some time

318
00:19:11.070 --> 00:19:12.420
to think about your answer.

319
00:19:22.950 --> 00:19:25.590
Okay, well done if you said false.

320
00:19:25.590 --> 00:19:27.120
So, this statement is false

321
00:19:27.120 --> 00:19:30.480
because although there is no exact legal definition

322
00:19:30.480 --> 00:19:32.100
of online harassment,

323
00:19:32.100 --> 00:19:36.060
it can still be prosecuted under a number of laws

324
00:19:36.060 --> 00:19:37.920
such as the Defamation Act

325
00:19:37.920 --> 00:19:40.350
if it makes the victim feel scared

326
00:19:40.350 --> 00:19:42.513
or concerned for their safety.

327
00:19:44.670 --> 00:19:46.890
Time for a task now.

328
00:19:46.890 --> 00:19:50.070
First, we're going to read the scenario below together,

329
00:19:50.070 --> 00:19:53.130
and then I would like you to offer advice to Aisha

330
00:19:53.130 --> 00:19:55.473
on what to do and what not to do.

331
00:19:56.790 --> 00:20:01.080
Aisha says, "Recently, I have seen lots of comments online

332
00:20:01.080 --> 00:20:04.140
about women who wear the hijab.

333
00:20:04.140 --> 00:20:06.810
They are full of offensive stereotypes

334
00:20:06.810 --> 00:20:09.297
and it is really upsetting me to see."

335
00:20:11.070 --> 00:20:14.670
Then I would like you to discuss this question below.

336
00:20:14.670 --> 00:20:17.970
It says, "What are the potential consequences

337
00:20:17.970 --> 00:20:20.907
for online harassment in this scenario?"

338
00:20:22.230 --> 00:20:25.290
Pause the video so you can have some time to do the tasks,

339
00:20:25.290 --> 00:20:27.993
and then we can go through the answers together.

340
00:20:32.220 --> 00:20:34.320
Okay, well done for having a go.

341
00:20:34.320 --> 00:20:37.927
So, your advice to Aisha could include,

342
00:20:37.927 --> 00:20:40.080
"Aisha should block and report the accounts

343
00:20:40.080 --> 00:20:43.620
making the offensive comments on the site she's using

344
00:20:43.620 --> 00:20:45.870
via their built-in tools.

345
00:20:45.870 --> 00:20:49.170
She should tell a trusted adult she has witnessed this

346
00:20:49.170 --> 00:20:51.780
and if she knows the victim in person,

347
00:20:51.780 --> 00:20:54.810
she could reach out to them for support.

348
00:20:54.810 --> 00:20:57.120
She should not retaliate to the people

349
00:20:57.120 --> 00:21:00.840
who are posting hurtful comments and harassing others,

350
00:21:00.840 --> 00:21:05.840
as this can escalate the situation and make things worse."

351
00:21:05.880 --> 00:21:08.180
Well done if you said something similar to me.

352
00:21:09.570 --> 00:21:11.520
For the second part of your task,

353
00:21:11.520 --> 00:21:14.130
you had to discuss the potential consequences

354
00:21:14.130 --> 00:21:17.010
for online harassment in this scenario.

355
00:21:17.010 --> 00:21:19.357
So, your answer could include,

356
00:21:19.357 --> 00:21:22.560
"If the harassment makes a person feel unsafe

357
00:21:22.560 --> 00:21:25.230
and concerned for their physical safety,

358
00:21:25.230 --> 00:21:28.050
it can be considered unlawful behaviour

359
00:21:28.050 --> 00:21:30.060
under several different laws,

360
00:21:30.060 --> 00:21:32.820
including the Malicious Communications Act

361
00:21:32.820 --> 00:21:35.040
and the Defamation Act.

362
00:21:35.040 --> 00:21:38.370
If the harassment online involves hate speech,

363
00:21:38.370 --> 00:21:41.430
it can be considered unlawful if it incites

364
00:21:41.430 --> 00:21:45.210
hatred or violence towards a person or group,

365
00:21:45.210 --> 00:21:48.510
and can result in a prison sentence.

366
00:21:48.510 --> 00:21:50.883
Well done if your answer was similar to mine.

367
00:21:53.610 --> 00:21:55.890
This brings us to the end of our lesson.

368
00:21:55.890 --> 00:21:58.740
Here is a summary of everything that we've covered today.

369
00:21:59.850 --> 00:22:02.850
Although the internet can be a positive space,

370
00:22:02.850 --> 00:22:06.510
some people may use it as a tool to harass others

371
00:22:06.510 --> 00:22:09.030
or spread hate speech.

372
00:22:09.030 --> 00:22:12.273
This is an unacceptable use of the internet.

373
00:22:13.110 --> 00:22:15.270
If we ever witness or experience

374
00:22:15.270 --> 00:22:17.850
harassment or hate speech online,

375
00:22:17.850 --> 00:22:21.390
we should report and block the offending account.

376
00:22:21.390 --> 00:22:25.470
We should also tell a trusted adult as soon as possible.

377
00:22:25.470 --> 00:22:27.240
We should never retaliate,

378
00:22:27.240 --> 00:22:29.283
as this can make the situation worse.

379
00:22:30.510 --> 00:22:33.690
If the harassment makes a person feel unsafe

380
00:22:33.690 --> 00:22:37.050
or their comments promote hate speech and violence,

381
00:22:37.050 --> 00:22:39.870
it can be considered unlawful behaviour

382
00:22:39.870 --> 00:22:43.533
and be punishable with either a fine or imprisonment.

383
00:22:48.120 --> 00:22:49.740
Here's a slide with different places

384
00:22:49.740 --> 00:22:51.480
that you can get support.

385
00:22:51.480 --> 00:22:52.890
We have the Childline,

386
00:22:52.890 --> 00:22:54.540
which is a website and phone line

387
00:22:54.540 --> 00:22:58.560
which is able to offer confidential advice and support.

388
00:22:58.560 --> 00:23:00.570
We have the CEOP.

389
00:23:00.570 --> 00:23:02.460
The CEOP helps protect children

390
00:23:02.460 --> 00:23:05.550
from online abuse and exploitation.

391
00:23:05.550 --> 00:23:07.410
And the Internet Matters.

392
00:23:07.410 --> 00:23:09.930
The Internet Matters teaches children and parents

393
00:23:09.930 --> 00:23:13.863
how to stay safe and happy online while using the internet.

lessons.unitTitle: Our online lives: How can I stay in control online?

lessonKeywords.description: a person who self-identifies as an 'involuntary celibate' and believes that they are unable to form romantic or sexual relationships, often blaming women for this
hatred or prejudice against women, often shown through negative beliefs or actions
the process by which someone comes to adopt extreme political, social or religious views
when an adult builds trust with a young person to manipulate them for harmful purposes, often leading to abuse or exploitation

keyLearningPoints.keyLearningPoint: 'Incel' means 'involuntary celibate' and is a term linked to online communities that promote hatred towards women.
Incel ideology promotes violence, blame and extreme beliefs.
Grooming often starts with trust-building, then isolation and manipulation.
Radicalisers use coded language and emotional manipulation to influence others.
There are ways to stay safe, such as questioning content, talking to trusted adults and reporting harmful behaviour.

misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.response: Radicalisation can affect anyone, regardless of social status or popularity. It's essential to understand behaviours, not stereotypes, to identify risks accurately.
misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.misconception: Only socially isolated or unpopular individuals become radicalised.

lessons.pupilLessonOutcome: I can explain what incel ideology is, identify the dangers associated with it, and describe strategies to protect myself and others from radicalisation.

teacherTips.teacherTip: The content of this lesson is sensitive. Please speak to your RSHE Lead and/or DSL before teaching this lesson.

Today's lesson outcome is, "I can explain what incel ideology is and identify the dangers associated with it, and describe strategies to protect myself and others from radicalisation." Let's begin by taking a look at our ground rules together.
Laura says we should listen to others.
It's okay to disagree with each other, but we should listen properly before making assumptions or deciding how to respond.
When disagreeing, challenge the statement and not the person.
Andeep says we should respect privacy.
This means we can discuss examples, but we mustn't use names or descriptions that identify anyone including ourselves.
Izzy says, "Choose your level of participation.
Everyone has the right to choose not to answer a question or join discussion.
We must never put anyone on the spot." And Jacob says, "No judgement.
We can explore beliefs and misunderstandings about a topic without fear of being judged." All of these ground rules are here to keep everyone safe throughout the lesson.
Here are some of today's key words.
We have incel, misogyny, and radicalisation.
And incel means a person who self identifies as an involuntary celibate and believes that they are unable to form romantic or sexual relationships, often blaming women for this.
Misogyny means hatred or prejudice against women, often shown through negative beliefs or actions.
And radicalisation means the process by which someone comes to adopt extreme political, social, or religious views.
And the final keyword for this lesson is grooming.
Grooming is when an adult builds trust with a young person to manipulate them for harmful purposes, often needing to abuse or exploitation.
Keep an eye out for these keywords as they are going to pop up throughout today's lesson.
Here is the lesson's outline, and we are going to begin with what are incels and their dangers.
Incel stands for involuntary celibate.
Typically, incels are men who express frustration and resentment about their lack of romantic or sexual relationships.
The term celibate means a person who chooses not to have sexual relationships, often for religious or personal reasons.
However, in the context of incel, the term is used differently.
Incels claim their celibacy is involuntary rather than a personal choice.
Common beliefs of incels are entitlement to relationships, blaming women and girls for their lack of sexual or romantic relationships, hostility towards gender equality.
And incels use coded language and means to communicate their beliefs and identify others who share their views.
This allows them to spread harmful ideas whilst appearing less obviously threatening to outsiders.
Time for a check for understanding.
Which of the following are common beliefs for incels? Is it A, entitlement to relationships, B, blaming women and girls, or C, accepting of gender equality? Which of the following are common beliefs for incels? Pause this video so you can have some time to think about your answer.
Well done if you said A and B.
Entitlement to relationships and blaming women and girls are common beliefs for incels.
Incel ideology has been linked to multiple incidents of violence, including attacks motivated by misogynistic beliefs.
These incidents demonstrate how online hatred can translates into a real-world harm, affecting not just the individuals that are involved, but entire communities.
People who follow in incel ideologies may experience severe emotional and psychological distress, such as loneliness, depression, and despair.

How can we spot grooming and radicalisation? People with incel beliefs often don't work alone.

Online grooming may involve manipulating trust online to influence someone towards harmful or extremist views.
Those who carry out online grooming often target vulnerabilities, offering false friendship or validation.
Those who engage in online grooming exploits people's insecurities.
They make use of platforms such as online forums, social media, and messaging apps.
They often use flattery, offer gifts, and try to isolate the person being groomed from their friends and family.
Police Officer Kofi says, "Anyone can be groomed or radicalised online regardless of their background, intelligence, social status, or family situation.
Radicalisation often targets normal human emotions and experiences such as feeling left out, disappointed, or going through difficult times, which makes it something that could potentially affect anyone." Police Officer Kofi says, "Those who engage in online grooming and radicalisation use specific tactics to influence their targets.
These tactics work because they prey on normal human needs for belonging, understanding, and validation.
Understanding these methods can help you recognise when someone might be trying to manipulate you or someone you know." Common manipulation tactics include love bombing, which means showering someone with excessive attention, compliments, and support to make them feel special and valued.
It also includes creating an us versus them mentality, convincing someone that only certain people understand them, whilst everyone else, such as family, friends, and society, is against them.
Gradual escalation.
This means slowly introducing more extreme ideas over time so the person doesn't notice how far their thinking has shifted.
Exploiting vulnerabilities.
That means targeting people during difficult times in their lives.
And offering simple solutions.

Signs that someone is being radicalised online include withdrawing from their family, friends, and activities, expressing extreme or hostile views, using coded language or referring to extremist ideas, spending increasing amounts of time in specific online communities or forums, and becoming defensive or secretive about their online activities and conversations.

Develop critical thinking skills.
Ask yourself, "Who benefits from this message? What evidence supports these claims? And are there any other perspectives that I shouldn't consider?" Recognising your emotional triggers.
Understand what makes you feel vulnerable.
It could be stress, loneliness, rejection, and be extra cautious about new online relationships during these times.
And practise digital wellness.
That means taking regular breaks from social media and forums, especially if they're making you feel angry or isolated.

lessons.unitTitle: Power in relationships: What do we need to know about the law?

lessonKeywords.description: unwanted words, actions or behaviours of a sexual nature that make someone uncomfortable, upset or afraid

keyLearningPoints.keyLearningPoint: Harmful sexual behaviour (HSB) is inappropriate sexual behaviour which is harmful and abusive.
Sexual violence can escalate and begin as sexist jokes or comments.
90% of girls and nearly 50% of boys have been sent explicit pictures or videos of things they did not want to see.
There are laws to protect people from harmful sexual behaviour.
Harmful sexual behaviour can take different forms, including: harassment, upskirting, coercion and manipulation.

misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.response: Whilst the age of consent is 16, it is illegal to take, have or share sexual imagery of anyone under the age of 18.
misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.misconception: It is acceptable to take, have or share sexual imagery of anyone over the age of 16.

lessons.pupilLessonOutcome: I can describe what harmful sexual behaviour is, explain the law around it and explain where to get support.

teacherTips.teacherTip: You may want to work with your RSHE or DSL lead to adapt this lesson to the needs of your school and community before delivery.

lessons.unitTitle: Power in relationships: What do we need to know about the law?

lessonKeywords.description: unwanted sexual actions that hurt, pressure or make others feel unsafe or uncomfortable

keyLearningPoints.keyLearningPoint: Harmful sexual behaviour (HSB) can happen in person or online and is never acceptable.
It is important to listen, show support, and never blame the person affected.
You should report harmful behaviour, even if it feels difficult.
Trusted adults and services can help keep everyone safe.

misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.response: Telling a trusted adult about something serious someone else has done isn’t about getting anyone in trouble, it’s about keeping yourself and others safe.
misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.misconception: I will get into trouble if I disclose something that someone else has done.

lessons.pupilLessonOutcome: I can explain how to support others involved in difficult times and when and how to seek help.

teacherTips.teacherTip: Make sure pupils know how to report concerns in your setting.

Hi, I'm Ms. Lowe, and I'm your RSHE teacher for today.
Thank you so much for choosing to complete your learning with me.

And because of the themes and the topics that we're gonna cover today in this lesson, it's important that you complete your learning with the company of an adult.

So Laura is reminding us that in RSHE, we should listen to others.
It's okay to disagree with each other, but we should listen properly before making assumptions or deciding how to respond.

Andeep is reminding us to respect privacy.
We can discuss examples, but we don't use names or descriptions that can identify anyone, including ourselves.

We're gonna begin today's lesson by asking the question, why is harmful sexual behaviour so serious? So harmful sexual behaviour, or HSB, refers to unwanted sexual behaviours that are inappropriate, non-consensual, or abusive.
HSB can happen in person or online.
And these behaviours may include things like making sexual jokes or comments, pressuring someone into touching or sexual activity, sharing nudes or semi-nudes without permission.
And repeated unwanted flirting or messages.

There are so many different trusted adults that we have in our lives who are there to protect us from any harmful behaviours that we might encounter.

Social worker Natalie says, "Hey, you might notice someone becoming quieter, more withdrawn.

when someone repeatedly bothers, bullies or disturbs another person, making them feel unsafe, uncomfortable or upset

keyLearningPoints.keyLearningPoint: The law protects us from online threats like harassment, grooming and image sharing.
Personal information should be kept private to stay safe online.
If something online feels wrong or uncomfortable, it's important to tell a trusted adult.
Blocking, reporting and privacy settings help protect us and others online.

misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.response: Even if you delete something you have shared online, others may have saved or shared it. Think before posting online and speak to a trusted adult if you make a mistake or feel unsafe.
misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.misconception: If I delete something online, no one can find it or see it.

lessons.transcript_sentences:
Hi, I'm Miss Lowe and I'm your RSHE teacher for today.
Thank you so much for choosing to complete your learning with me.
Today's lesson is all about Protecting myself online and seeking support.
And because of the themes and the topics that we're gonna cover today in this lesson, it's important that you complete your learning with the company of an adult.
By the end of today's lesson, you are gonna be able to explain how you can protect yourself online and how you can seek support.
Every RSHE lesson should begin with a set of ground rules.
This ensures that every conversation had in RSHE is respectful and we're all able to learn effectively.
So Laura is reminding us that in RSHE we should listen to others.
"It's okay to disagree with each other, but we should listen properly before making assumptions or deciding how to respond.
And when disagreeing, we challenge the statement and not the person." Andeep is reminding us to respect privacy.
"We can discuss examples, but we don't use names or descriptions that can identify anyone, including ourselves." Izzy is reminding us to choose a level of participation that suits us.
"Everyone has the right to choose not to answer a question or to join in a discussion, but we never put anyone on the spot." And finally, Jacob is reminding us that in RSHE there is no judgement.
"We can explore beliefs and misunderstandings about a topic without the fear of being judged." So let's start by having a look at our keywords for today's lesson.
First, we have grooming.
This is when an adult builds trust with a young person to manipulate them for harmful purposes, often leading to abuse or exploitation.
Harassment: when someone repeatedly bothers, bullies or disturbs another person, making them feel unsafe, uncomfortable, or upset.
We're gonna begin today's lesson by asking the question, what risks and laws relate to being online? So lots of young people go online every single day and they do that because it can be a really fun and useful way to talk with friends, family, loved ones to learn new things, to try new skills, and to share.
However, it's important to note that not everyone online has good intentions or motivations behind being online.
And if we are able to understand the risks that we may face online, it can help keep us and others safe.
So Laura is telling us here that when she's online, she talks to her friends.
She's never really thought about what could go wrong when she's doing that.
But there are real risks to being online.
And these risks include: receiving unwanted or pressuring messages, it could involve seeing, upsetting or harmful content, being contacted by strangers, being asked to keep secrets, or being pressured to share images or personal information.
So Ethan here is talking to Emily and he says, "I've encountered risks online.
For instance, someone I don't know once messaged me saying they knew my school.
It felt really strange." Emily says here, "Me too.

keyLearningPoints.keyLearningPoint: Criminal exploitation involves manipulating and using individuals for criminal activities.
Child Sexual Expoitation (CSE) and Child Criminal Exploitation (CCE) are very serious.
County lines is a method of drug trafficking that exploits vulnerable individuals.
There are sometimes signs that someone is a victim of exploitation.

Hello, my name's Miss Willow, and I'm going to be your teacher for today's lesson.
Today's lesson is called "Power and Consent," and it fits into the unit "Power in Relationships: How Can We Keep Safe?" During this lesson, we are going to be talking about sexual content and other sensitive content, too, so for this lesson, we require you to have an adult with you.
If you don't have an adult with you at the moment, please come back to this lesson when you do have one with you.

Next, Izzy says that we can choose our level of participation.
