Hello, I'm Miss Tee, and welcome to today's lesson.
Today we're talking about safety in the sun, and that's part of our unit on Staying safe and healthy: How can I check my body is healthy? Our lesson outcome for today is: I can explain how to keep myself safe in the sun, what sun damage looks like, and what to do about it.
Before we get started on today's lesson, it's really important that we think about the ground rules that we follow when we're having discussions in our classrooms. We've got Laura firstly saying, "Listen to others.
It's okay to disagree with each other, but we should listen properly before making assumptions or deciding how to respond.
And when we disagree, we challenge the statement.
We don't challenge the person." We've got Jacob saying, "No judgment.
We can explore beliefs and misunderstandings about a topic without fear of being judged." Andeep tells us to respect privacy.
He says, "We can discuss examples, but we do not use names or descriptions that could identify anyone, including ourselves." And finally, Izzy reminds us to choose the level of participation that is right for us.
Everyone has the right to choose not to answer a question or join a discussion.
We never put anyone on the spot.
So with those in mind, let's get started with today's lesson.
Let's take a look at the keywords that we're going to be using in this lesson.
We've got five keywords.
The first one is melanoma, which is a serious type of skin cancer that starts in cells that make skin color.
It can spread to other body parts if not caught early.
Then we have ultraviolet, also referred to as UV, which are invisible light rays mainly from the sun that cause sunburn and can damage skin over time.
Then we have infrared, also shortened to IR, which are invisible light rays that can be felt as heat.
They come from the sun, warm objects, and are used in remote controls and night vision.
We also have the phrase fake tan, which is a cosmetic product that temporarily darkens your skin to look tanned without sun exposure.
And finally, mole.
And in this context, it's a small, usually dark spot on your skin made of clustered pigment cells.
Most are harmless, but changes in size or color need checking.
As we go through our lesson today, see where these words are being used and see if you can use them in your own responses.
We've got two lesson outlines for today's lesson on safety in the sun.
Firstly, how can I stay safe in the sun? And secondly, what are the signs of skin cancer? So let's start with our first lesson outline, how can I stay safe in the sun? When the weather gets warmer, it's nice to spend more time outside and to enjoy the sunshine.
But Dr. Elsie says, "Being in the sun has lots of health benefits.
It increases our serotonin, which helps boost our mood.
Our skin also uses sunlight to make vitamin D, which improves immunity and regulates our circadian rhythm, helping us to get better quality sleep." However, too much sun, especially without protection, can cause sunburn, premature skin aging, increased risk of melanoma.
And Dr. Elsie says that being safe in the sun is important at all ages, but younger skin can burn more easily because it has a thinner outer layer, making it more sensitive to the sun's ultraviolet, or UV, rays.
There are two main types of UV rays emitted from the sun.
These are UVA and UVB.
UVA rays have longer wavelengths that can affect deeper layers of skin and are linked to skin aging, wrinkles, and some skin cancers.
UVB rays have shorter wavelengths, and these are primarily responsible for sunburn and melanomas.
The sun also emits infrared, IR, light.
IR light is a different type of ray that is lower in energy.
IR light warms the skin.
Although not as strong as UV light, it can still cause burns or skin irritation.
Feeling too hot can cause someone to overheat, become dehydrated, or suffer from heat stroke.
So to protect ourselves from the effects of the sun, we should wear sun cream, stay cool, drink water, wear light layers.
Izzy says, "I love the summer because we get to play outdoors more.
However, we only need to worry about protecting ourselves from the sun when it's really hot and we can feel the temperature." But Dr. Elsie replies and says, "Sun damage can occur in the UK from March to October, even when the sun does not feel warm.
This is because although we can't feel the sun or when it is cloudy, invisible UV rays can still pass through the atmosphere and burn our skin." Sunburn is your skin's reaction to too much UV radiation from the sun.
UV rays damage the skin's outer layers, causing inflammation, pain, and redness.
Dr. Elsie says that sunburn makes the body react by sending more blood to the area, and this causes that redness.
Although this visual sign may be harder to see on darker skin, other signs like the skin feeling hot, tight, or painful indicates sun damage.
And in some cases, skin may blister or peel.
The best way to protect yourself from sunburn is to apply sun cream and stay covered up as much as possible.
Sun cream should be applied before you go out and then again every two hours and also applied anytime after swimming or being in the water.
Laura says, "There are lots of different types of sun cream.
How do I know which one to use?" And Dr. Elsie replies, "Sun creams are rated by sun protection factors called SPF, and these can range from factor 2 to factor 50+.
A sun cream that is factor 50+ offers the greatest protection as it blocks out more of the sun's UV rays.
For children and teenagers, 50+ is recommended for all skin types as anyone can get sunburn or be at risk of skin cancer.
So in this check for understanding, can you identify when sunscreen should be applied? Is it every hour, every two hours, twice a day, or only after being in the water? Pause your screen while you think about your answer.
Well done.
If you said that sun cream should be applied every two hours, then you'd be correct.
Well done.
So it's important that any sun cream we use is at least SPF 30, although 50 is recommended for children.
That it also has at least a 4+ star UVA protection rating.
"SPF means sun protection factor," says Izzy.
And the UV rating measures the amount of ultraviolet protection.
Even if the sun cream says waterproof or water-resistant, you should still always reapply after swimming or being in the water.
A UV index is like a weather forecast, and you can tell how strong the UV rays are on any given day by looking at this.
In addition to using sun cream, you can also stay safe in the sun by covering up and wearing clothes or UV protective fabrics such as UV suits or rash vests.
You can also stay safe by wearing a hat to protect the top of your head.
A wide-brimmed hat is better than a baseball hat because this also protects the back of your neck.
You can also wear sunglasses to protect your eyes.
You can limit how long you spend in the sunshine and stay in the shade between 11 and 3 when the sun is the hottest.
Dr. Elsie says, "Remember, whenever you spend time in warm weather, stay hydrated by drinking plenty of water." When you are out in the sun, an easy way to remember what to do is slip, slop, slap.
This is to slip on a shirt, slop on sun cream, and slap on a hat.
This message was part of a safety campaign encouraging people to protect themselves from the sun, because even one burn can cause lasting sun damage.
So in this check for understanding, can you identify which child is best protected from UV rays on a day at the beach? Pause your screen while you think about your answer.
Well done.

We can see that they've got a shirt on, trousers on, and a wider-brimmed hat.
Some people want to have a tan but do not want to risk going in the sun to achieve this, so they might opt for a fake tan instead.
This is done by using fake tanning cream or lotion, and it's a cosmetic process that temporarily darkens the skin without sun exposure.
If you're using fake tan, always try a patch test first to check for any allergies to ingredients.
Fake tan is generally considered to be safe because it does not involve exposure to UV rays.
However, some individuals may experience skin irritation or allergic reactions.
They may also find that it creates dry skin.
Some people might use sunbeds.
Now, sunbeds are machines that give off UV rays to tan skin.
This light is the same as sunlight, but is much stronger and more concentrated.
Sunbeds can be extremely dangerous because they give off UVA and UVB rays that damage skin.
Risks of using a sunbed include getting burnt, developing wrinkles and sun spots, a significant increase in developing melanoma.
In the UK, it is illegal for anyone under the age of 18 to use a sunbed.
So in this check for understanding, true or false? Using a sunbed can significantly increase someone's chances of developing melanoma.
Pause your screen while you think about your answer.
If you identified that the answer was true, then you'd be correct.
Well done.
So in task A, Jun has been asked by his teacher to make a poster outlining how to stay safe in the sun.
Can you help Jun create his poster by including the following information: what you should wear to protect yourself in the sun, how you can manage your time in the sun, and other tips on how to stay safe in the sun? Pause your screen while you think about your answer.
So your sun safety poster may look like this and include sun safety tips such as seek shade, wear a hat, use sunscreen, limit your sun time, stay hydrated, wear protective clothing, and use sunglasses.
And it may also have included the following information.
Sun cream should be applied every two hours and always after swimming.
You should always use a sun cream with SBF 50+.
You should always follow the slip, slop, slap rule.
You should stay out of the sun between 11 and 3 as this is when the sun is hottest.
And you should remember that sunbeds should not be used by anyone under the age of 18.
So let's move on to our second lesson outline for today, what are the signs of skin cancer? Dr. Elsie says, "It's important that we check our bodies regularly for any signs of being unwell, and this includes checking our skin for any symptoms of sun damage." The first sign of sun damage is that the skin is red, tight, hot, painful, blistering, or peeling.
And if this happens, you should stay out of the sun and cover up, take a cool shower, drink plenty of water, use a moisturizer or aloe vera gel to soothe the skin, and take painkillers under the supervision of an adult if needed.
Dr. Elsie also says that if sunburn continues to be painful, if it blisters or becomes infected, if it's severe, or if it's on a child or infant, it's important to seek medical help.
Your pharmacist or local GP can help to recommend treatments and give advice.
Dr. Elsie also said that it's not just sunburn that can indicate sun damage.
Signs of skin cancer or other long-term conditions caused by the sun can often be spotted by noticing changes in moles, spots, or freckles on your skin.
It's important to check your skin regularly.
Skin cancer can happen to anyone, even young people.
And spotting the signs early makes a big difference.
Most people have freckles or moles on their skin.
These are normally harmless, but it is important to keep an eye on them in case they change, as this can be an indicator of a melanoma.
Freckles are small, light brown, or reddish spots that often cluster together on areas of the skin that get the most sun.
Whereas moles are larger colored spots that may be flat or protruding from the skin.
Using the ABCDE rule can be helpful to remember the key characteristics of moles that may indicate melanoma.
A is for asymmetry.
B is for border irregularity.
C is for color.
D is for diameter.
And E is for evolving.
So if you notice that the mole is asymmetrical, meaning the two halves are not the same shape, if you notice that it has an irregular or blurred border edge, if you notice that it has multiple colors, so maybe shades of black, white, gray, brown, or pink, if you notice that it has a diameter of more than six millimeters or that it is evolving, which means growing or changing in size, shape, or color, then you should see your doctor to have this investigated.
So in this check for understanding, what does the B stand for in the ABCDE mole checking guide? Is it A, bumpy; B, brown; C, border; or D, blurry? Pause your screen while you think about your answer.
If you identified that the answer was C, B is for border, then you'd be correct, well done.
Dr. Elsie says that if you notice any changes to your skin, moles, or freckles, if you notice any new moles, lumps, or growths, or if you find anything that you're worried about, you should tell a trusted adult and see a doctor.
Normally, there is nothing to be concerned about, but early detection of any health condition improves the success of treatment that might be needed.
Dr. Elsie says that when you see a doctor about a mole, freckle, or spot on your skin, they will first do a visual exam and check your skin.
And this may include looking at moles through a special tool called a dermatoscope.
A dermatoscope is a magnifying piece of equipment with light that helps the doctor see the skin in more detail.
It shows patterns and colors under the surface that aren't visible to the naked eye.
If a doctor thinks something needs further investigation, then they may request a biopsy.
A biopsy is when a small sample of skin is sent to a laboratory where it's closely examined under a microscope to see if any cells are cancerous.
Jacob says, "What happens during a biopsy?" And Dr. Elsie replies, "A biopsy is a very quick procedure and is done with local anesthetic to numb the area.
If you are under 18, you will need to have a parent or guardian with you for the procedure.
Or if you are over 18, you can request to have someone with you during the procedure." Usually, the results of a biopsy are back within a few days or weeks, depending on the urgency of the referral.
It can feel worrying for people while they wait.
But remember, often these tests are just used to rule out anything that might be more serious, and early diagnosis will significantly improve outcomes.
If you have any questions, you should always ask your doctor.
So let's come to our final check for understanding.

It's important to check your skin regularly for any unusual changes.
You can use the ABCDE rule to help spot signs of skin cancer.
A is for asymmetry, which means the two halves of A mole don't match.

So in summary.
Today's lesson on safety in the sun.
To stay safe in the sun, you should never let yourself get sunburnt.
Being burnt just once can cause serious skin damage.
The sun emits damaging ultraviolet, UV, and infrared, IR, rays.
Wearing sun cream, wearing a hat, and covering up can help to protect your skin.
Apply sun cream before you go out, every two hours, and after swimming.

keyLearningPoints.keyLearningPoint: Most cancers are more treatable the earlier they're detected, regular examinations are important.
Most abnormalities aren't cancer, but it is important to get them checked.
Breast cancer is most common in people over 50. People of any gender can get breast cancer.

keyLearningPoints.keyLearningPoint: Understanding water risks helps prevent accidents and drowning.
Cold water shock can happen even in warm weather.
Alcohol and peer pressure increase risks around water.
Lifesaving techniques and emergency services can save lives.
Knowing how to assess a situation is key to staying safe.

So on our final lesson outline for today,

lessonKeywords.description: the process of becoming immune or resistant to a disease, usually through a vaccine
the process of receiving a vaccine, for example, receiving the injection, or taking an oral or nasal dose
disease-fighting proteins that play a crucial role in the immune system; they recognise infectious invaders, such as bacteria and viruses, and help the body destroy them
contain weakened versions of viruses or bacteria, giving long-term protection
contain viruses or bacteria that have been destroyed, or just parts of them; several doses or a booster are needed for full protection

keyLearningPoints.keyLearningPoint: Vaccines protect against deadly diseases.
Vaccines are thoroughly tested before being used.
Vaccines do not contain anything harmful, only ingredients to make them work.
Vaccines have made deadly diseases like smallpox, polio and tetanus, rare or eliminated in the UK.
If people stop having vaccines, it's possible for infectious diseases to quickly spread again.

misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.response: Vaccinations are offered by health professionals at different ages.
misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.misconception: You only have vaccinations as a baby or young child.

lessons.pupilLessonOutcome: I can explain the benefits of immunisation and evaluate the arguments around them.

teacherTips.teacherTip: You may wish to work with your local public health team to time delivering this lesson at the same time that pupils might receive vaccinations.

lessons.unitTitle: Staying safe and healthy: How can I check my body is healthy?

lessonKeywords.description: in this context, continuing to exist or endure over a prolonged period
when something is not normal for you; this could be something that changes suddenly or over time
sudden, quick or sometimes severe
persistent for a long time, or recurring

keyLearningPoints.keyLearningPoint: It is important to know what is normal for your body and watch out for changes that don't go away after two weeks.
Weight loss or gain without trying is a sign of a potential problem.
Persistent tiredness is a cause for concern.
If you experience changes to your bowel habits you should seek medical support.
If you experience pain, abnormal bleeding or discharge from any area of the body you should seek medical support.

misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.response: While serious symptoms are important, early or mild signs, like changes in sleep, appetite, or energy, can also signal a health issue. It’s best to notice and act early by speaking to a trusted adult or health professional.
misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.misconception: Only serious symptoms, like fainting or chest pain, mean something is wrong.

lessons.pupilLessonOutcome: I can describe the bodily signs that signal a potential health issue and explain what to do if I spot them.

teacherTips.teacherTip: Encourage pupils to take all health concerns seriously, remind them that even small or vague symptoms are worth noticing and talking about with a trusted adult.

because symptoms that are chronic

lessons.unitTitle: Risky substances: What do I need to know about tobacco and vaping?

lessonKeywords.description: a thin stick of tobacco wrapped in paper that people smoke; it's bad for health and can cause many serious diseases
a plant used in cigarettes that contains nicotine and produces harmful smoke when burned
an electronic device filled with chemicals that creates an aerosol which is breathed in
an addictive drug that cigarettes and some vapes contain
if something is addictive, it makes you want to keep using it or doing it, even if it is not good for you

keyLearningPoints.keyLearningPoint: Smoking is the act of burning cigarettes (tobacco products) and inhaling the smoke.
Vapes are devices that allow you to inhale nicotine in a vapour rather than smoke.
Most vapes and all tobacco products contain nicotine, which is a highly addictive substance.
People may begin smoking or vaping due to peer pressure, because they think it looks 'cool' or as a way to relax.
There are multiple UK laws intended to reduce the number of people smoking and vaping.

misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.response: In fact, the majority of young people in the UK don't smoke or vape. In 2023, less than 1% of 11-15 year olds reported regular smoking and less than 9% regularly vape.
misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.misconception: Many pupils believe that the majority of their peers are smoking or vaping.

lessons.pupilLessonOutcome: I can explain what smoking and vaping are and the laws surrounding them.

teacherTips.teacherTip: This lesson has recently been updated to reflect the changes in the law as a result of the Tobacco and Vapes Act 2026.

lessons.transcript_sentences:
Hello, my name is Mr. Wells, and welcome to today's RSHE lesson, called "Smoking and Vaping." It's part of the unit "Risky Substances: What Do I Need to Know About Tobacco and Vaping?" Before we get started, I should advise you that you should have an adult with you when you are completing this lesson.
Let's make a start.
Today's lesson outcome is: I can explain what smoking and vaping are and the laws surrounding them.
As with every RSHE lesson, there are a number of ground rules, so let's take a moment to go through them together.
Laura says, "We should listen to others.
It's okay to disagree with each other, but we should listen properly before making assumptions or deciding how to respond.
When disagreeing, we should challenge the statement rather than the person." Andeep says, "We should respect privacy.
We can discuss examples, but we should not use names or descriptions that identify anyone, including ourselves." Jacob says that there should be no judgment.
"We can explore beliefs and misunderstandings about a topic without the fear of being judged." And finally, Izzy says that we should choose our level of participation.
"Everyone has the right to choose not to answer a question or join discussion, and we should never put anybody on the spot." Throughout today's lesson, there are a number of key words.
We're going to see them throughout the lesson in bold.
Let's take a moment to understand what they mean.
Cigarette: a thin stick of tobacco wrapped in paper that people smoke.
It's bad for health and can cause many serious diseases.
Tobacco: a plant used in cigarettes that contains nicotine and produces harmful smoke when burned.
Nicotine: an addictive drug that cigarettes and some vapes contain.
Addictive: if something is addictive, it makes you want to keep using it or doing it, even if it's not good for you.
And finally, vape: an electronic device filled with chemicals that creates an aerosol, which is breathed in.
Today's lesson, "Smoking and Vaping," is in three parts.
The first is: What is smoking? The second is: What is vaping? And finally: What is the law around smoking and vaping? Let's make it start with our first learning cycle.
What is smoking? Cigarettes are sticks of shredded tobacco, and it begins as a tobacco plant.
It's then dried and rubbed, and it's made into cigarettes.
Smoking is the act of burning tobacco and inhaling the smoke.
When tobacco is burned, it releases nicotine, along with other substances.
And nicotine is a highly addictive substance.
Addiction can happen only after days of infrequent inhalation of nicotine.
When nicotine is inhaled, it causes dopamine to be released in the brain.
And dopamine is a feel-good chemical, but the effects are temporary.
The brain begins to crave this feeling, and this can lead to an addiction.
Nicotine is a stimulant.
A stimulant is a substance that speeds up messages between the brain and the body.
And effects of stimulants like nicotine include feeling more awake or alert and temporary improvement in concentration.
These effects are short-lived and wear off quickly.
And when the effects wear off, people may feel tired, irritable, or anxious.
This can make them want to use the stimulant again, which is how addiction develops.
When a cigarette is lit, nicotine and other chemicals are inhaled.
There are around 70 carcinogenic, cancer-causing substances within cigarette smoke, including tar, arsenic, and carbon monoxide.
It's time for our first check for understanding.
What is the highly addictive substance in cigarettes? Is it A, tobacco; B, nicotine; or C, tar? The correct answer is B, nicotine.
Well done if you got that right.
People might choose to smoke for a variety of reasons.
Some people believe that it relieves stress and improves mood.
They might smoke because of peer pressure: their friends are telling them they should do.
And because of smoking in the family, or due to a nicotine addiction.
Nicotine has some immediate but short-term effects that people might enjoy.
These short-term effects can have long-term consequences.
They might cause a sense of relaxation, but over time, cigarettes cause cravings.
They might feel that cigarettes are relieving stress, but over time, withdrawal from cigarettes creates stress.
And they might feel that it improves their concentration.
But over time, brain function actually declines.
Young people may start smoking as a way to fit in, and peer pressure to smoke may come from friends or from seeing people online or in the media smoking.
However, the large majority of the UK population does not smoke, especially young people.
Dr Elsie shares an important statistic with us.
She says that, "In 2023, less than 12% of the UK population were smokers.
And less than 1% of 11 to 15-year-olds reported regular smoking." It's time for our next check for understanding.
True or false: the majority of the UK population smokes.
Is that true, or is it false? The correct answer is false, and I wonder if you can tell me why.
Well, the majority, 88% in 2023, of the UK population does not smoke.
It's time for our first task.
I would like you to label the image of the cigarette with what it contains and facts about smoking that you have learned in this learning cycle.
The first one has been done for you.
And you can see there's an image of a cigarette, and it says, "Cigarettes contain nicotine and tobacco." You can pause the screen now, complete the task, and, when you're ready to go through the answers, press play.
Let's take a look at your answers together.
You were asked to label the image of the cigarette with what it contains and facts about smoking that you have learned in this learning cycle.
Your answers could include: less than 12% of the UK population smokes.
The short-term effects lead to long-term health consequences.
Cigarettes contain nicotine and tobacco.
People may start smoking due to peer pressure.
Any good feelings from cigarettes are short-term, and cigarettes contain harmful substances such as tar and arsenic.
You might have more ideas around your cigarette as well, and that's absolutely fantastic.
Well done for all your hard work so far.
It's already time for our second learning cycle.
What is vaping? Vapes are electronic devices, and most contain nicotine and simulate smoking by allowing nicotine to be inhaled through an aerosol, often called vapor, rather than smoke.
Vapes work by heating a liquid known as e-liquid.
E-liquid often contains nicotine; vegetable glycerin, a sweet liquid that creates the aerosol; propylene glycol, a liquid that carries the flavor; flavorings.
And unlike cigarettes, vapes don't contain tar or carbon monoxide.
People may choose to vape for a variety of reasons: to help them quit smoking cigarettes; because they enjoy the different flavorings; due to peer pressure; because nicotine is addictive and stopping can cause withdrawal symptoms; and because they've seen others vape online and in the media.
People might start vaping as a way of trying to stop smoking cigarettes.
Vapes can allow smokers to still get nicotine without breathing in the tar and carbon monoxide found in cigarette smoke.
However, all vapes come with risks to health, such as breathing difficulties.
Even nicotine-free vapes contain chemicals that can harm your lungs when heated and inhaled.
Many of the long-term risks of vaping are still unknown because vapes haven't been around long enough for scientists to study their effects over many years.
It's time for our next check for understanding.
True or false? "All vapes contain nicotine, so they are harmless." Is that true, or is it false? The correct answer is false.
And I wonder if you can tell me why.
Well, it's false because not all vapes contain nicotine, though most do.
And vapes are not harmless.
The chemicals and vapes can damage your lungs when heated and inhaled, causing problems like breathing difficulties.
Vapes are often advertised as having fun and appealing flavors and coming packaging that is often brightly colored and attractive.
Many people think vapes are harmless because of this.

lessonKeywords.description: an addictive drug that cigarettes and some vapes contain

keyLearningPoints.keyLearningPoint: Smoking introduces harmful and risky substances like tar, nicotine and carbon monoxide into the body.
Vapes contain ingredients found in everyday items, but when inhaled through a vape can be harmful to health.
Illegal vapes can be extremely dangerous and hard to spot.

misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.response: Vaping is not harmless as vapes contain nicotine and other chemicals that can harm the lungs and cause addiction, especially in young people.
misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.misconception: Vaping is harmless.

Illegal vapes are particularly dangerous because they can contain banned substances like lead or dangerous levels of nicotine.
And you can spot an illegal vape by checking the nicotine strength, puff count, and health warning coverage.
It's always good to know where you could get further support.
You might reach out to the NHS Live Well website, which offers advice about healthy living, exercise, quitting smoking, and drinking less alcohol, or Childline, a website and phone line which is able to offer confidential advice and support.
Well done for all your hard work today.
And I hope you join us soon for another Oak National Academy lesson.

are a, the UK government has banned the use

255
00:13:01.050 --> 00:13:03.090
of certain substances in vapes,

256
00:13:03.090 --> 00:13:06.930
and c, they can contain much higher levels of nicotine

257
00:13:06.930 --> 00:13:08.373
than legal vapes allow.

258
00:13:10.050 --> 00:13:11.643
It's time for our next task.

259
00:13:13.050 --> 00:13:15.570
I want you to imagine you work for a health and safety team

260
00:13:15.570 --> 00:13:18.150
that investigates vape ingredients.

261
00:13:18.150 --> 00:13:21.510
Two vapes have been sent to you for analysis.

262
00:13:21.510 --> 00:13:23.250
Write a brief report for each vape,

263
00:13:23.250 --> 00:13:24.900
identifying which ingredients

264
00:13:24.900 --> 00:13:27.450
could be harmful and explain why.

265
00:13:27.450 --> 00:13:29.580
For each vape, you should identify

266
00:13:29.580 --> 00:13:33.690
which ingredients are found in legal and illegal vapes,

267
00:13:33.690 --> 00:13:36.633
explain why certain ingredients could be harmful,

268
00:13:37.470 --> 00:13:41.703
and state which vape poses a greater risk to health and why.

269
00:13:42.900 --> 00:13:47.550
Vape A, the red vape, contains vegetable glycerin,

270
00:13:47.550 --> 00:13:52.550
strawberry flavoring, and nicotine at 2%.

271
00:13:52.650 --> 00:13:57.650
The blue vape, Vape B, contains vegetable glycerin,

272
00:13:58.350 --> 00:14:02.183
pentanedione, and nicotine at 5%.

273
00:14:03.180 --> 00:14:05.400
You can pause the screen now and press play

274
00:14:05.400 --> 00:14:07.650
when you're ready to go through your answers.

275
00:14:13.620 --> 00:14:16.110
You were asked to write a brief report for each vape

276
00:14:16.110 --> 00:14:18.240
identifying which ingredients could be harmful

277
00:14:18.240 --> 00:14:19.950
and explain why.

278
00:14:19.950 --> 00:14:21.873
Your report could look like this.

279
00:14:22.740 --> 00:14:25.140
Vape A contains vegetable glycerin,

280
00:14:25.140 --> 00:14:28.380
which is found in legal vapes and skincare products.

281
00:14:28.380 --> 00:14:32.400
However, when heated and inhaled, it can harm the lungs.

282
00:14:32.400 --> 00:14:34.230
The strawberry flavoring is safe in food

283
00:14:34.230 --> 00:14:38.250
but creates harmful compounds when heated in a vape.

284
00:14:38.250 --> 00:14:40.620
Nicotine at 2% is the legal limit,

285
00:14:40.620 --> 00:14:42.093
but it is still addictive.

286
00:14:43.170 --> 00:14:45.600
Vape B is much more dangerous.

287
00:14:45.600 --> 00:14:47.370
It contains pentanedione,

288
00:14:47.370 --> 00:14:50.250
a chemical linked to serious lung disease.

289
00:14:50.250 --> 00:14:52.560
The nicotine level is 5%,

290
00:14:52.560 --> 00:14:55.830
which is above the legal 2% limit.

291
00:14:55.830 --> 00:14:59.520
Overall, Vape B is an example of an illegal vape

292
00:14:59.520 --> 00:15:01.380
and poses a much greater risk

293
00:15:01.380 --> 00:15:03.750
because it contains banned substances

294
00:15:03.750 --> 00:15:05.643
and dangerous levels of nicotine.

295
00:15:08.730 --> 00:15:09.780
You're doing really well,

296
00:15:09.780 --> 00:15:12.330
and we're now onto our third learning cycle,

297
00:15:12.330 --> 00:15:14.790
how can we spot an illegal vape?

298
00:15:14.790 --> 00:15:17.760
It's important to know how to recognize illegal vapes

299
00:15:17.760 --> 00:15:20.640
because they can be particularly dangerous.

300
00:15:20.640 --> 00:15:23.520
There's different ways to spot an illegal vape.

301
00:15:23.520 --> 00:15:26.973
Legal vapes contain no more than 2% nicotine.

302
00:15:27.960 --> 00:15:30.180
30% of the packaging on a legal vape

303
00:15:30.180 --> 00:15:32.463
is covered by a health warning risk.

304
00:15:33.480 --> 00:15:37.230
And a legal vape can contain a maximum of 600 puffs,

305
00:15:37.230 --> 00:15:39.603
equal to around 50 cigarettes.

306
00:15:40.710 --> 00:15:43.920
With legal vapes, the contents of the vape are regulated,

307
00:15:43.920 --> 00:15:46.353
with most harmful chemicals banned.

308
00:15:48.240 --> 00:15:49.950
Illegal vapes, on the other hand,

309
00:15:49.950 --> 00:15:53.040
contain more than 2% nicotine.

310
00:15:53.040 --> 00:15:54.090
They will have little

311
00:15:54.090 --> 00:15:56.670
to no health warnings on the packaging.

312
00:15:56.670 --> 00:15:59.820
They may contain as many as 4,000 puffs,

313
00:15:59.820 --> 00:16:03.240
which is more than six times the legal limit.

314
00:16:03.240 --> 00:16:06.600
And the contents of illegal vapes are not regulated,

315
00:16:06.600 --> 00:16:10.533
meaning it can contain deadly substances such as lead.

316
00:16:12.630 --> 00:16:15.630
Take a look at the packaging for this vape.

317
00:16:15.630 --> 00:16:18.480
This packaging contained an illegal vape

318
00:16:18.480 --> 00:16:23.250
because it contains 5% nicotine

319
00:16:23.250 --> 00:16:25.230
and 4,000 puffs,

320
00:16:25.230 --> 00:16:29.703
whereas the legal limit is 2% nicotine and 600 puffs.

321
00:16:31.050 --> 00:16:35.160
It doesn't have a health warning covering 30% of the packet.

322
00:16:35.160 --> 00:16:37.620
And it says chemical rather than substance,

323
00:16:37.620 --> 00:16:39.960
as chemical is used in other countries

324
00:16:39.960 --> 00:16:42.453
where the same rules do not apply to vapes.

325
00:16:43.830 --> 00:16:46.320
It's time for our next check for understanding.

326
00:16:46.320 --> 00:16:49.230
Which of the following is a sign that a vape is illegal?

327
00:16:49.230 --> 00:16:53.490
A, 30% of the packaging is covered in a health warning,

328
00:16:53.490 --> 00:16:56.910
b, it contains more than 2% nicotine,

329
00:16:56.910 --> 00:17:00.630
or c, the vape contains 600 puffs,

330
00:17:00.630 --> 00:17:03.123
equal to around 50 cigarettes.

331
00:17:07.950 --> 00:17:11.970
The correct answer was b, it contains more than 2% nicotine.

332
00:17:11.970 --> 00:17:13.570
Well done if you got that right.

333
00:17:15.090 --> 00:17:16.950
The substances in illegal vapes

334
00:17:16.950 --> 00:17:19.560
can cause nicotine poisoning

335
00:17:19.560 --> 00:17:21.780
due to very high nicotine levels,

336
00:17:21.780 --> 00:17:25.620
causing rapid heartbeat, nausea, or even seizures,

337
00:17:25.620 --> 00:17:30.183
contain illegal drugs such as tetrahydrocannabinol, THC,

338
00:17:31.080 --> 00:17:33.480
a substance found in cannabis,

339
00:17:33.480 --> 00:17:36.150
contain dangerous levels of substances like lead,

340
00:17:36.150 --> 00:17:39.210
which damages the brain and nervous system,

341
00:17:39.210 --> 00:17:42.510
and chromium which can cause lung disease.

342
00:17:42.510 --> 00:17:44.430
It is particularly dangerous for young people

343
00:17:44.430 --> 00:17:46.590
to use vapes with high nicotine content

344
00:17:46.590 --> 00:17:48.270
because young people's brains and bodies

345
00:17:48.270 --> 00:17:49.680
are still developing,

346
00:17:49.680 --> 00:17:52.140
and nicotine can affect brain development.

347
00:17:52.140 --> 00:17:56.163
In the UK, it is illegal to sell vapes to anyone under 18.

348
00:17:57.420 --> 00:17:59.850
Retailers must verify age

349
00:17:59.850 --> 00:18:03.210
and can be fined if they sell vape products to minors

350
00:18:03.210 --> 00:18:06.423
or allow adults to buy on behalf of minors.

351
00:18:07.350 --> 00:18:09.810
This is called proxy purchasing.

352
00:18:09.810 --> 00:18:13.473
Both the retailer and the adult can face legal consequences.

353
00:18:14.610 --> 00:18:17.850
Trading Standards officers carry out spot checks

354
00:18:17.850 --> 00:18:21.180
and test purchases to ensure shops are following the law.

355
00:18:21.180 --> 00:18:23.340
These laws are in place to protect young people

356
00:18:23.340 --> 00:18:26.250
from the harmful effects of nicotine and vaping.

357
00:18:26.250 --> 00:18:28.410
And Police Officer Kofi tells us

358
00:18:28.410 --> 00:18:30.660
that selling a vape to someone under 18

359
00:18:30.660 --> 00:18:34.893
is punishable with a fine of up to 2,500 pounds.

360
00:18:36.210 --> 00:18:39.300
If someone offers you a cigarette, vape, or illegal vape,

361
00:18:39.300 --> 00:18:41.940
you have the right to say no.

362
00:18:41.940 --> 00:18:44.587
Ways of saying no could look like,

363
00:18:44.587 --> 00:18:47.017
"No thanks, I'm not interested,"

364
00:18:47.017 --> 00:18:48.727
"It's not for me,"

365
00:18:48.727 --> 00:18:51.513
"No thanks," and you just don't need to give a reason.

366
00:18:52.410 --> 00:18:54.480
If you need support, talk to a trusted adult,

367
00:18:54.480 --> 00:18:58.260
like a parent, carer, teacher, or school nurse,

368
00:18:58.260 --> 00:19:01.050
or you could contact Childline for free.

369
00:19:01.050 --> 00:19:03.840
Remember, you're in control of your choices,

370
00:19:03.840 --> 00:19:05.280
and choosing to protect your health

371
00:19:05.280 --> 00:19:07.620
is always the right decision.

372
00:19:07.620 --> 00:19:09.750
It's time for a check for understanding.

373
00:19:09.750 --> 00:19:11.040
True or false.

374
00:19:11.040 --> 00:19:13.770
It is dangerous for young people to use illegal vapes

375
00:19:13.770 --> 00:19:16.770
because their brains and bodies are still developing.

376
00:19:16.770 --> 00:19:18.933
Is that true or is it false?

377
00:19:23.670 --> 00:19:25.203
The correct answer is true.

378
00:19:26.340 --> 00:19:28.743
It's time for our final task of today's lesson,

379
00:19:29.640 --> 00:19:32.190
write one paragraph answering the question,

380
00:19:32.190 --> 00:19:35.520
why are illegal vapes particularly dangerous

381
00:19:35.520 --> 00:19:37.320
compared to legal vapes?

382
00:19:37.320 --> 00:19:39.120
Your answer should try to include

383
00:19:39.120 --> 00:19:41.520
how to identify an illegal vape,

384
00:19:41.520 --> 00:19:43.890
at least three different ways,

385
00:19:43.890 --> 00:19:47.010
the specific dangers of illegal vapes,

386
00:19:47.010 --> 00:19:50.550
and why they're especially harmful to young people.

387
00:19:50.550 --> 00:19:52.200
I'd like you to pause the screen now

388
00:19:52.200 --> 00:19:55.200
and press play when you're ready to go through your answers.

389
00:20:00.930 --> 00:20:02.460
It's time to go through your answers.

390
00:20:02.460 --> 00:20:04.440
Your paragraph might include:

391
00:20:04.440 --> 00:20:07.230
illegal vapes can be identified in three ways.

392
00:20:07.230 --> 00:20:09.480
They contain more than 2% nicotine,

393
00:20:09.480 --> 00:20:13.950
as the legal limit is 2%, they have more than 600 puffs,

394
00:20:13.950 --> 00:20:16.560
as the legal limit is only 600 puffs,

395
00:20:16.560 --> 00:20:20.220
or the health warning does not cover 30% of the packaging.

396
00:20:20.220 --> 00:20:21.690
Illegal vapes are more dangerous

397
00:20:21.690 --> 00:20:23.550
because they're not regulated.

398
00:20:23.550 --> 00:20:26.100
They can contain deadly substances like lead,

399
00:20:26.100 --> 00:20:28.320
which are banned in the UK.

400
00:20:28.320 --> 00:20:30.900
They can also contain dangerous levels of nicotine

401
00:20:30.900 --> 00:20:33.420
that can cause nicotine poisoning.

402
00:20:33.420 --> 00:20:35.730
These vapes are especially harmful for young people

403
00:20:35.730 --> 00:20:38.520
because their brains and bodies are still developing,

404
00:20:38.520 --> 00:20:41.400
and high nicotine levels can affect brain development

405
00:20:41.400 --> 00:20:42.633
and cause addiction.

406
00:20:43.560 --> 00:20:46.410
Well done if your answer looks something like that.

407
00:20:46.410 --> 00:20:48.390
Well done for your work in today's lesson.

408
00:20:48.390 --> 00:20:49.890
You've worked really hard.

409
00:20:49.890 --> 00:20:51.000
We're going to take a moment now

410
00:20:51.000 --> 00:20:52.600
to summarize what we've learned.

411
00:20:53.490 --> 00:20:55.170
Smoking cigarettes is risky

412
00:20:55.170 --> 00:20:58.020
because they contain harmful substances such as nicotine,

413
00:20:58.020 --> 00:21:01.353
which is addictive, and tar, which damages the lungs.

414
00:21:02.400 --> 00:21:06.450
Cigarettes also contain toxic chemicals found in rat poison,

415
00:21:06.450 --> 00:21:08.403
car exhaust fumes, and batteries.

416
00:21:09.990 --> 00:21:12.600
Vaping is risky because vapes contain chemicals

417
00:21:12.600 --> 00:21:16.320
that, when heated and inhaled, can damage the lungs.

418
00:21:16.320 --> 00:21:18.633
Many vapes also contain nicotine.

419
00:21:19.560 --> 00:21:21.270
Illegal vapes are particularly dangerous

420
00:21:21.270 --> 00:21:23.310
because they can contain banned substances

421
00:21:23.310 --> 00:21:26.073
like lead or dangerous levels of nicotine.

422
00:21:27.090 --> 00:21:28.770
And you can spot an illegal vape

423
00:21:28.770 --> 00:21:31.590
by checking the nicotine strength, puff count,

424
00:21:31.590 --> 00:21:33.273
and health warning coverage.

425
00:21:34.110 --> 00:21:34.980
It's always good to know

426
00:21:34.980 --> 00:21:36.780
where you could get further support.

427
00:21:37.800 --> 00:21:40.770
You might reach out to the NHS Live Well website,

428
00:21:40.770 --> 00:21:43.410
which offers advice about healthy living, exercise,

429
00:21:43.410 --> 00:21:45.960
quitting smoking, and drinking less alcohol,

430
00:21:45.960 --> 00:21:48.510
or Childline, a website and phone line

431
00:21:48.510 --> 00:21:51.750
which is able to offer confidential advice and support.

432
00:21:51.750 --> 00:21:53.700
Well done for all your hard work today.

433
00:21:53.700 --> 00:21:55.170
And I hope you join us soon

434
00:21:55.170 --> 00:21:57.393
for another Oak National Academy lesson.

lessons.unitTitle: Risky substances: What do I need to know about tobacco and vaping?

a decision that contributes to physical and mental wellbeing

keyLearningPoints.keyLearningPoint: Smoking, vaping and using nicotine products are linked to serious health concerns.
Making healthy choices benefits physical and mental health; quitting smoking or vaping are examples of healthy choices.
Smoking, vaping and using nicotine products can impact a person socially.
Saying no assertively rather than aggressively can help challenge peer pressure safely and respectfully.

misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.response: Smoking affects multiple body systems, increasing the risk of heart disease, strokes and respiratory illnesses.
misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.misconception: Smoking only affects the lungs.

lessons.pupilLessonOutcome: I can describe the physical and social impacts of smoking, vaping and using nicotine products and explain how best to say no to peer pressure.

teacherTips.teacherTip: Consider role-playing appropriate scenarios to help pupils practise saying no assertively. Emphasise the difference between assertive (calm, clear) and aggressive (hostile) refusal. Remind pupils that real friends respect boundaries and that it's always ok to walk away from pressure.

Hello, my name's Ms. Mello and I'm going to be your teacher for today's lesson.
Today's lesson is called The Impact of Smoking and Vaping, and it fits into the unit risky substances.
What do I need to know about tobacco and vaping? During this lesson, we are going to be talking about some sensitive content, so for this lesson, we recommend you have an adult with you.
If at any point during this lesson you feel worried or uncomfortable, it's really important that you stop the lesson and that you speak to a trusted adult.
Okay, let's make a start.
By the end of today's lesson, you'll be able to describe the physical and social impacts of smoking, vaping and using nicotine products, and you'll be able to explain how best to say no to peer pressure.
Before we get started with today's lesson, we need to go over some ground rules.
These help to make sure that everyone feels safe and comfortable during today's lesson.
Laura says that we need to listen to others.

Next, Izzy says that we can choose our level of participation.

Finally, Jacob reminds us that we need to not have any judgment.
We can explore any beliefs and misunderstandings that you have about a topic without fear of being judged by others.
We're now going to take a look at the keywords for today's lesson.
Our first keyword is nicotine.
This is an addictive drug that cigarettes and some vapes contain.
Next, we have healthy choice.
This is a decision that contributes to physical and mental wellbeing, and finally, we have peer pressure.
This is when you feel pushed by friends to act a certain way, make choices or do things just to fit in with the group.
Today's lesson is split into three learning cycles.
Our first learning cycle is called What are the Health Risks of Smoking and Vaping? Our second learning cycle is called What is the Social Impact of Smoking and Vaping? And finally, our last learning cycle is called, How Can I Respectfully Say No? Let's make a start on our first learning cycle.
What are the health risks of smoking and vaping? The harmful substances in cigarettes such as tar and arsenic damage multiple parts of the body.
This can lead to several serious long-term illnesses, including at least 16 different types of cancer, including lung, throat, bladder, kidney, and stomach cancer.
It can also lead to chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, often called COPD.
It can also lead to heart disease.
Smoking can also cause hypertension, which is high blood pressure, strokes, asthma, and it can also cause harm to reproductive health.
It can also cause diabetes and blindness or cataracts.
It can also cause decline in brain function.
There are lots of different health risks of smoking.
According to NHS England 2024, in the UK, 72% of lung cancer cases are caused by smoking.
We're now going to talk about how smoking damages the lungs.
When someone smokes, chemicals are inhaled through cigarette smoke.
The chemicals damage cells in the lungs so that they can't work properly.
Sometimes damaged cells divide abnormally, and this can create a cancerous growth.

I'd like you to decide if the statement is true or false.

Talk to the people around you or have a think to yourself.
Well done if you said that this is false, but why? You might have said that smoking damages multiple parts of the body, not just the lungs.
It can cause heart disease, strokes, several types of cancer and many other serious illnesses too.
Well done if you said something like this.
Several substances in cigarettes can put pressure on your heart and this can cause damage.
Dr. Elsie says that even inhaling the smoke from someone else's cigarette, which is known as passive smoking can damage the heart.
According to the British Heart Foundation, at least 15,000 people die from smoking related heart and circulatory diseases each year in the UK.
That's around 40 people every day.
We're now going to talk about how smoking damages the heart.
Nicotine increases blood pressure and damages artery walls, chemicals in smoke cause fatty deposits to build up in the damaged arteries.
These deposits make it harder for oxygen-rich blood to reach the heart and the brain, and over time arteries become clogged and can cause a heart attack or a stroke.
Let's do another check for understanding.
Which of the following statements about heart disease are inaccurate, so not true.
A, chemicals in smoke leave fatty deposits in the arteries.
B, passive smoking can't damage the heart or C, smoking can lead to heart attacks and strokes.
Which of those statements about heart disease are inaccurate? Pause the video, talk to the people around you or have a think to yourself.
Well done if you said that B is correct.
It's not true that passive smoking doesn't damage the heart.
Passive smoking, so breathing in someone else's cigarette smoke can cause damage to the heart.
Well done if you remember this.
When someone makes a healthy choice to quit smoking, it can drastically improve their health.
It can improve their life expectancy by around 10 years.
It can lower the risk of different cancers, it can increase their energy levels.
It can improve their sense of smell and taste, and it can lower the risk of heart disease and strokes.
Quitting smoking can also improve someone's mental health.
Many people think smoking helps them cope with stress, but nicotine withdrawal actually causes the stress and anxiety that smoking temporarily relieves.
Dr. Elsie says that therefore quitting smoking can lead to lower levels of anxiety, depression, and stress, resulting in improved mood and a better quality of life for the person that's quit smoking.
Let's do another check for understanding.
I'd like you to tell your partner three reasons why quitting smoking is a healthy choice.
Pause the video and talk to people around you or how think to yourself.
You might have said any of the following.
It improves life expectancy.
It lowers the risk of cancer, increases energy, improves senses, lowers the risk of heart disease and strokes, and it improves mental health.
Well done if you said any of these three reasons about why quitting smoking is a healthy choice.
Vaping is considered less harmful than smoking, but it isn't risk-free.
Vapes can contain harmful chemicals that affect the lungs and heart when heated and inhaled.
Many of the long-term health risks of vaping are still unknown, meaning that it could be more harmful than we currently know.
For young people, vaping is especially risky as nicotine can harm the developing brain and make it harder to concentrate or sleep, which is really important for young people especially.
If you don't smoke, the NHS advises not to start vaping because of the possible health risks and risk of addiction, so the known health risks of vaping are breathing problems, coughing and wheezing, headaches, lung damage, mouth and throat irritation and nausea.
This means feeling sick.

lessons.lessonTitle: Getting support to give up smoking or vaping
lessons.unitTitle: Risky substances: What do I need to know about tobacco and vaping?

lessonKeywords.description: an addictive drug that cigarettes and some vapes contain
a loss of control over doing, taking or using something even when it is harmful
the actions taken to help someone who is in a difficult or dangerous situation, such as providing care and seeking medical attention

keyLearningPoints.keyLearningPoint: Quitting smoking or vaping helps the body recover and feel healthier.
Nicotine addiction can make quitting difficult, but support helps.
Using NHS or local stop-smoking services makes quitting more successful.
Cravings and mood changes are normal when giving up nicotine.
Trusted adults and professionals can guide and encourage quitting safely.

misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.response: Nicotine is addictive, which means quitting alone can be very hard. Support from trusted adults, NHS services or community advisers gives people practical help and encouragement, making success much more likely.
misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.misconception: People should be able to stop smoking or vaping on their own.

lessons.pupilLessonOutcome: I can describe what happens when someone quits smoking or vaping, and explain how support makes it easier to stop.

teacherTips.teacherTip: Use positive and supportive language — focus on health and recovery, not blame. Explain that vaping can help adults who already smoke, but it’s not safe or needed for children.

00:11:12.630 --> 00:11:14.910
It's time for the second learning cycle.

233
00:11:14.910 --> 00:11:17.073
Where can someone get help to quit?

234
00:11:17.940 --> 00:11:19.650
People are three times more likely

235
00:11:19.650 --> 00:11:22.773
to quit successfully when they get support.

236
00:11:23.790 --> 00:11:27.300
Support helps people understand their cravings.

237
00:11:27.300 --> 00:11:28.920
Stay motivated.

238
00:11:28.920 --> 00:11:31.350
Find safe ways to cope.

239
00:11:31.350 --> 00:11:33.570
Make a plan that works for them,

240
00:11:33.570 --> 00:11:37.860
and manage difficult feelings like irritability or low mood

241
00:11:37.860 --> 00:11:41.343
and get back on track if they have a setback.

242
00:11:43.380 --> 00:11:46.380
Dr. Elsie says that, "No one has to quit alone.

243
00:11:46.380 --> 00:11:49.020
There is help and support available for everyone,

244
00:11:49.020 --> 00:11:50.970
whether it's the first time they're trying to quit

245
00:11:50.970 --> 00:11:52.440
or the 20th.

246
00:11:52.440 --> 00:11:54.330
Support gives people the tools

247
00:11:54.330 --> 00:11:56.430
and encouragement to keep going

248
00:11:56.430 --> 00:11:58.617
whatever nicotine product they're using."

249
00:12:00.930 --> 00:12:05.070
Nurse Daniel is here from the NHS Stop Smoking Service,

250
00:12:05.070 --> 00:12:08.940
and they offer free friendly ways to support anyone

251
00:12:08.940 --> 00:12:10.113
who wants to quit.

252
00:12:11.850 --> 00:12:15.720
They can give advice and check progress,

253
00:12:15.720 --> 00:12:18.090
provide free resources and apps,

254
00:12:18.090 --> 00:12:20.283
and help people plan their quit journey.

255
00:12:24.210 --> 00:12:25.290
Local pharmacies

256
00:12:25.290 --> 00:12:28.740
and health clinics can also help people quit.

257
00:12:28.740 --> 00:12:32.850
So pharmacists like pharmacist Harper are trained to

258
00:12:32.850 --> 00:12:34.950
offer advice about cravings,

259
00:12:34.950 --> 00:12:38.410
provide nicotine replacement options like nicotine patches

260
00:12:39.300 --> 00:12:42.513
and signposts to other services to support.

261
00:12:45.120 --> 00:12:47.280
It's time for a check for understanding.

262
00:12:47.280 --> 00:12:48.600
True or false.

263
00:12:48.600 --> 00:12:50.340
A pharmacist can support someone

264
00:12:50.340 --> 00:12:53.190
who is trying to give up smoking or vaping.

265
00:12:53.190 --> 00:12:54.753
Is that true or false?

266
00:13:00.510 --> 00:13:01.953
The correct answer is true.

267
00:13:03.030 --> 00:13:04.383
You might have thought why?

268
00:13:11.010 --> 00:13:12.960
And the reason is because pharmacists

269
00:13:12.960 --> 00:13:15.090
are healthcare professionals.

270
00:13:15.090 --> 00:13:17.943
Anyone can ask them for help or information.

271
00:13:20.430 --> 00:13:23.040
At school, support for quitting smoking

272
00:13:23.040 --> 00:13:26.280
or vaping might come from the school nurse,

273
00:13:26.280 --> 00:13:27.330
a trusted teacher,

274
00:13:27.330 --> 00:13:29.190
the pastoral or wellbeing team,

275
00:13:29.190 --> 00:13:32.520
a Designated Safeguarding Lead or DSL

276
00:13:32.520 --> 00:13:33.933
or a school counselor.

277
00:13:35.310 --> 00:13:38.250
These staff members are trained to help and won't judge.

278
00:13:38.250 --> 00:13:40.170
They keep conversations confidential

279
00:13:40.170 --> 00:13:42.630
unless they're worried about your safety.

280
00:13:42.630 --> 00:13:44.340
You can talk to them about yourself

281
00:13:44.340 --> 00:13:45.990
or someone you are worried about.

282
00:13:48.030 --> 00:13:50.460
Ms. Walsh is the Designated Safeguarding Lead

283
00:13:50.460 --> 00:13:52.327
for her school and she says that,

284
00:13:52.327 --> 00:13:53.790
"If a pupil or family member

285
00:13:53.790 --> 00:13:55.830
wants to give up nicotine products,

286
00:13:55.830 --> 00:13:58.530
I can help them find the right support.

287
00:13:58.530 --> 00:14:00.090
I can link them with our school nurse

288
00:14:00.090 --> 00:14:01.680
or local health services

289
00:14:01.680 --> 00:14:04.440
and make sure they get trusted advice.

290
00:14:04.440 --> 00:14:06.090
You don't have to manage it alone.

291
00:14:06.090 --> 00:14:08.847
I'm here to help you get the help you need."

292
00:14:09.690 --> 00:14:12.663
There are free confidential services anyone can use.

293
00:14:13.650 --> 00:14:17.340
Such as the NHS Smokefree Helpline 0300 123 1044.

294
00:14:20.250 --> 00:14:23.613
Childline on 0800 1111,

295
00:14:24.858 --> 00:14:27.540
and the NHS Quit Smoking app.

296
00:14:27.540 --> 00:14:30.033
You might also use Talk to FRANK.

297
00:14:30.960 --> 00:14:33.300
And these give tips, daily encouragement,

298
00:14:33.300 --> 00:14:35.463
and someone to talk to when it's hard.

299
00:14:38.070 --> 00:14:41.400
Josephine works as a charity helpline worker,

300
00:14:41.400 --> 00:14:44.040
helping people who ring her for support

301
00:14:44.040 --> 00:14:46.680
when they're trying to give up smoky or vaping.

302
00:14:46.680 --> 00:14:49.050
And she says, "When someone calls us,

303
00:14:49.050 --> 00:14:52.410
we listen and help them make a plan to quit.

304
00:14:52.410 --> 00:14:53.730
We talk through cravings,

305
00:14:53.730 --> 00:14:55.770
give tips for handling stress

306
00:14:55.770 --> 00:14:59.490
and send follow up texts or links to free tools.

307
00:14:59.490 --> 00:15:02.823
Our job is to support people step by step.

308
00:15:05.970 --> 00:15:07.417
Nurse Daniel says,

309
00:15:07.417 --> 00:15:09.960
"Most people need more than one try,

310
00:15:09.960 --> 00:15:11.250
and that's okay.

311
00:15:11.250 --> 00:15:14.220
Research shows that people who use support services

312
00:15:14.220 --> 00:15:16.710
are much more likely to succeed

313
00:15:16.710 --> 00:15:19.410
even if it takes a few attempts.

314
00:15:19.410 --> 00:15:22.470
Each try is progress and not failure.

315
00:15:22.470 --> 00:15:24.597
The important thing is to keep trying."

316
00:15:27.090 --> 00:15:29.220
It's time for a check for understanding.

317
00:15:29.220 --> 00:15:32.610
Dom wants to stop vaping but doesn't know where to start.

318
00:15:32.610 --> 00:15:34.800
Who could he talk to at school for help

319
00:15:34.800 --> 00:15:36.783
and what might they do to support him?

320
00:15:47.040 --> 00:15:49.927
Your answers might have looked like this.

321
00:15:49.927 --> 00:15:51.690
"Dom could talk to the school nurse,

322
00:15:51.690 --> 00:15:53.670
pastoral team or DSL.

323
00:15:53.670 --> 00:15:55.560
They could listen and give him information

324
00:15:55.560 --> 00:15:56.940
and connect him with services

325
00:15:56.940 --> 00:15:59.337
like the NHS Smokefree Helpline."

326
00:16:01.350 --> 00:16:03.270
It's time for a task now.

327
00:16:03.270 --> 00:16:05.700
Hamza's cousin has been vaping for a few years

328
00:16:05.700 --> 00:16:07.380
and now wants to stop.

329
00:16:07.380 --> 00:16:09.600
She says it's hard because she feels stressed

330
00:16:09.600 --> 00:16:11.760
and doesn't know where to start.

331
00:16:11.760 --> 00:16:14.763
Hamza wants to help but isn't sure what advice to give.

332
00:16:15.660 --> 00:16:18.960
Write a short advice message to Hamza explaining,

333
00:16:18.960 --> 00:16:22.770
where his cousin can get safe and trusted help to quit

334
00:16:22.770 --> 00:16:25.263
and what kind of support those services offer.

335
00:16:26.400 --> 00:16:28.440
You can pause the screen now and press play

336
00:16:28.440 --> 00:16:30.690
when you're ready to go through your answers.

337
00:16:38.740 --> 00:16:40.170
Okay, well done.

338
00:16:40.170 --> 00:16:41.610
Let's go through your answer

339
00:16:41.610 --> 00:16:43.807
and it might look something like this.

340
00:16:43.807 --> 00:16:47.310
"Your cousin could get help from the NHS Smokefree Helpline,

341
00:16:47.310 --> 00:16:49.410
which gives free and confidential advice

342
00:16:49.410 --> 00:16:50.913
about how to stop vaping.

343
00:16:51.990 --> 00:16:54.030
She could also visit her local pharmacy

344
00:16:54.030 --> 00:16:55.920
to talk to a school nurse

345
00:16:55.920 --> 00:16:58.350
who can explain safe ways to manage cravings

346
00:16:58.350 --> 00:17:00.033
and make a plan to quit.

347
00:17:01.020 --> 00:17:04.050
The NHS Quit Smoking app can send daily tips

348
00:17:04.050 --> 00:17:07.170
and track progress to help her stay motivated.

349
00:17:07.170 --> 00:17:10.440
These services are there to guide people step by step

350
00:17:10.440 --> 00:17:12.513
so they don't have to try quitting alone.

351
00:17:13.440 --> 00:17:15.390
You are being a great support to her

352
00:17:15.390 --> 00:17:17.697
by helping her take the first steps."

353
00:17:19.350 --> 00:17:22.080
Let's take a look at the final learning cycle.

354
00:17:22.080 --> 00:17:23.940
You're doing really well.

355
00:17:23.940 --> 00:17:26.883
How can we support others to make healthy choices?

356
00:17:29.370 --> 00:17:31.650
Support can mean listening without judgment.

357
00:17:31.650 --> 00:17:33.600
Saying something kind or encouraging,

358
00:17:33.600 --> 00:17:37.083
helping someone find the right advice or service.

359
00:17:38.760 --> 00:17:39.757
Emily says,

360
00:17:39.757 --> 00:17:41.730
"When my older brother wanted to quit smoking,

361
00:17:41.730 --> 00:17:44.550
I just listened and told him I was proud he was trying.

362
00:17:44.550 --> 00:17:46.890
I didn't lecture him or tell him what to do.

363
00:17:46.890 --> 00:17:49.530
I just let him know I was there for him.

364
00:17:49.530 --> 00:17:51.540
He told me later that my support really helped him

365
00:17:51.540 --> 00:17:53.307
keep going when it got difficult."

366
00:17:55.650 --> 00:17:58.743
And even small words can make a big difference.

367
00:18:00.510 --> 00:18:02.070
For example,

368
00:18:02.070 --> 00:18:03.810
you're doing really well.

369
00:18:03.810 --> 00:18:05.460
I'm proud of you.

370
00:18:05.460 --> 00:18:07.320
You can do this.

371
00:18:07.320 --> 00:18:09.510
Every day is progress.

372
00:18:09.510 --> 00:18:11.070
The key is to be positive,

373
00:18:11.070 --> 00:18:13.083
patient and nonjudgmental.

374
00:18:14.340 --> 00:18:18.810
Avoid saying things like just stop or it can't be that hard.

375
00:18:18.810 --> 00:18:21.300
Quitting nicotine is genuinely difficult

376
00:18:21.300 --> 00:18:22.980
and people need understanding,

377
00:18:22.980 --> 00:18:23.813
not pressure.

378
00:18:26.580 --> 00:18:28.650
It's time for a check for understanding.

379
00:18:28.650 --> 00:18:30.630
Write one example of something supportive

380
00:18:30.630 --> 00:18:33.933
you could say to someone trying to make a healthy choice.

381
00:18:40.890 --> 00:18:42.663
Your answers might look like this.

382
00:18:43.530 --> 00:18:44.820
You are doing great.

383
00:18:44.820 --> 00:18:47.343
I'm proud of how hard you are trying.

384
00:18:50.130 --> 00:18:52.267
Robyn's dad says,

385
00:18:52.267 --> 00:18:55.230
"My family's kind words kept me going.

386
00:18:55.230 --> 00:18:56.670
Every time I wanted to smoke,

387
00:18:56.670 --> 00:18:59.160
I remembered how proud they were.

388
00:18:59.160 --> 00:19:01.680
My daughter, Robyn, made me a card saying,

389
00:19:01.680 --> 00:19:02.910
you can do it, dad!

390
00:19:02.910 --> 00:19:05.880
And I kept it in my wallet.

391
00:19:05.880 --> 00:19:08.430
Looking at it when I had a craving reminded me

392
00:19:08.430 --> 00:19:09.897
why I was doing this."

393
00:19:12.900 --> 00:19:16.140
If someone is struggling to quit or feels low,

394
00:19:16.140 --> 00:19:17.823
they may need extra help.

395
00:19:19.080 --> 00:19:22.200
You can support them by helping them speak to

396
00:19:22.200 --> 00:19:24.840
a trusted adult, the school nurse,

397
00:19:24.840 --> 00:19:27.930
the Designated Safeguarding Lead or DSL,

398
00:19:27.930 --> 00:19:29.130
the pastoral team,

399
00:19:29.130 --> 00:19:32.730
the NHS Smokefree Helpline or another service.

400
00:19:32.730 --> 00:19:35.820
And remember, asking for help shows strength

401
00:19:35.820 --> 00:19:36.963
and not weakness.

402
00:19:39.510 --> 00:19:41.047
Josephine says,

403
00:19:41.047 --> 00:19:43.440
"Sometimes people need a bit more help,

404
00:19:43.440 --> 00:19:44.820
and that's what we are here for.

405
00:19:44.820 --> 00:19:47.670
Talking to us is an important first step.

406
00:19:47.670 --> 00:19:49.830
We are here to listen without judgment,

407
00:19:49.830 --> 00:19:51.690
help you make a realistic plan

408
00:19:51.690 --> 00:19:54.720
and support you through the tough moments.

409
00:19:54.720 --> 00:19:57.660
You can call us whether you are thinking about quitting,

410
00:19:57.660 --> 00:19:58.740
actively trying,

411
00:19:58.740 --> 00:20:00.783
or need help after a setback.

412
00:20:03.720 --> 00:20:06.300
It's time for another check for understanding.

413
00:20:06.300 --> 00:20:08.070
A friend's says quitting is too hard

414
00:20:08.070 --> 00:20:09.540
and wants to give up.

415
00:20:09.540 --> 00:20:10.473
What could you do?

416
00:20:17.670 --> 00:20:18.727
You might have said,

417
00:20:18.727 --> 00:20:20.790
"Remind them of how far they've come,

418
00:20:20.790 --> 00:20:23.907
listen and help them talk to a trusted adult or service."

419
00:20:26.070 --> 00:20:28.560
It's time for our final task.

420
00:20:28.560 --> 00:20:29.880
Sort the different examples

421
00:20:29.880 --> 00:20:31.350
of how someone might respond

422
00:20:31.350 --> 00:20:33.780
when a friend wants to quit smoking or vaping

423
00:20:33.780 --> 00:20:36.843
into the columns helpful and unhelpful.

424
00:20:38.520 --> 00:20:40.050
Listening when they talk.

425
00:20:40.050 --> 00:20:41.520
Laughing at their efforts.

426
00:20:41.520 --> 00:20:43.110
Saying, "You're doing great."

427
00:20:43.110 --> 00:20:46.080
Saying, "It can't be that hard to quit."

428
00:20:46.080 --> 00:20:49.080
Encouraging them to get from support services.

429
00:20:49.080 --> 00:20:51.930
Spending time in smoke and vape free places.

430
00:20:51.930 --> 00:20:54.213
Or smoking or vaping in front of them.

431
00:20:55.080 --> 00:20:56.370
You could pause the screen now.

432
00:20:56.370 --> 00:20:58.200
Complete the task and press play

433
00:20:58.200 --> 00:21:00.413
when you're ready to go through your answers,

434
00:21:08.280 --> 00:21:09.113
Well done,

435
00:21:09.113 --> 00:21:11.160
your completed columns should look like this.

436
00:21:11.160 --> 00:21:12.960
In the helpful column you should have,

437
00:21:12.960 --> 00:21:14.580
listening when they talk.

438
00:21:14.580 --> 00:21:16.140
Saying, "You're doing great."

439
00:21:16.140 --> 00:21:18.960
Spending time in smoke and vape free places.

440
00:21:18.960 --> 00:21:23.130
Encouraging them to get help from support services.

441
00:21:23.130 --> 00:21:24.600
And in your unhelpful column,

442
00:21:24.600 --> 00:21:26.940
you should have laughing at their efforts.

443
00:21:26.940 --> 00:21:29.040
Smoking or vaping in front of them.

444
00:21:29.040 --> 00:21:31.797
And saying, "It can't be that hard to quit."

445
00:21:34.020 --> 00:21:36.240
Well done for all of your hard work today.

446
00:21:36.240 --> 00:21:39.390
Let's take a moment to go through what we've learned.

447
00:21:39.390 --> 00:21:40.500
Cigarettes, vapes,

448
00:21:40.500 --> 00:21:43.890
nicotine pouches and snus all contain nicotine.

449
00:21:43.890 --> 00:21:46.320
A drug that can cause addiction.

450
00:21:46.320 --> 00:21:49.293
Quitting helps the body recover and feel stronger.

451
00:21:50.490 --> 00:21:52.410
People choose to quit for many reasons,

452
00:21:52.410 --> 00:21:54.660
including improving their health and fitness,

453
00:21:54.660 --> 00:21:56.810
saving money and protecting their families.

454
00:21:57.870 --> 00:21:59.190
Support from trusted adults

455
00:21:59.190 --> 00:22:02.400
and health services like the NHS Smokefree Helpline

456
00:22:02.400 --> 00:22:04.473
really helps people quit successfully.

457
00:22:05.550 --> 00:22:06.810
Listening, encouraging,

458
00:22:06.810 --> 00:22:08.670
and being kind can make a big difference

459
00:22:08.670 --> 00:22:10.893
to someone trying to make a healthy choice.

460
00:22:12.000 --> 00:22:14.160
No one has to quit alone and help

461
00:22:14.160 --> 00:22:16.233
and support are always available.

462
00:22:17.520 --> 00:22:19.980
It might be you want some further support

463
00:22:19.980 --> 00:22:21.600
following this lesson.

464
00:22:21.600 --> 00:22:24.480
You could access the NHS Live Well website,

465
00:22:24.480 --> 00:22:27.120
which is an NHS advice about healthy living,

466
00:22:27.120 --> 00:22:30.390
exercise, quitting smoking and drinking less alcohol.

467
00:22:30.390 --> 00:22:31.530
Or Childline,

468
00:22:31.530 --> 00:22:33.690
a website and phone line which is able to offer

469
00:22:33.690 --> 00:22:35.673
confidential advice and support.

470
00:22:36.690 --> 00:22:38.340
Well done for all your hard work today,

471
00:22:38.340 --> 00:22:40.380
and I hope you decide to join us again

472
00:22:40.380 --> 00:22:42.603
for another Oak National Academy lesson.

lessons.unitTitle: Staying safe and healthy: Forced marriage, FGM, hymenoplasty & virginity testing

lessonKeywords.description: the practice of altering or injuring female genitals for non-medical reasons
a tradition or custom observed by a particular community or society
organisations and resources available to help victims of harmful practices

keyLearningPoints.keyLearningPoint: FGM stands for female genital mutilation.
FGM has serious physical and psychological impacts.
There are legal protections to prevent FGM.
There are support services for victims, or potential victims of FGM.

misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.response: FGM is not mandated by any religion. It is a cultural practice, and many religious leaders condemn it.
misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.misconception: FGM is a religious practice.

lessons.pupilLessonOutcome: I can describe what female genital mutilation is and explain its impacts and where to get support in the UK.

teacherTips.teacherTip: Speak to your RSHE lead or DSL before teaching this lesson. Be mindful of FGM having different names in different languages, (lists of these can be found on charity websites).

lessons.unitTitle: Staying safe and healthy: Forced marriage, FGM, hymenoplasty & virginity testing

lessonKeywords.description: when someone is made to marry without their consent – including anyone under 18, anyone pressured or threatened, or anyone who cannot make that decision
forcing someone to do something against their will through threats, pressure or intimidation

keyLearningPoints.keyLearningPoint: A legal marriage in the UK is where both partners are over 18 and fully consent with no threats or coercion.
A forced marriage is where one or both people cannot or do not consent to the marriage.
In a forced marriage, pressure, threats or abuse are used to make someone marry.
Forced marriage is illegal in the UK and punishable by up to seven years in prison.
Concerns about forced marriage can be raised with a trusted adult, teacher or the police.

misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.response: Arranged marriages involve family support in choosing a partner, but both people freely consent. Forced marriage removes consent and involves pressure, threats or abuse.
misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.misconception: Forced marriages are the same as arranged marriages.

lessons.pupilLessonOutcome: I can explain forced marriage, the law relating to it, and where someone could access support if they are concerned.

teacherTips.teacherTip: Before delivering this lesson, consult with your RSHE lead or Designated Safeguarding Lead (DSL). They can provide guidance on handling sensitive questions, and may help you connect with local safeguarding teams or specialist organisations, such as the Forced Marriage Unit.

lessons.unitTitle: Staying safe and healthy: Forced marriage, FGM, hymenoplasty & virginity testing

lessonKeywords.description: a medically invalid and harmful procedure that attempts to determine whether a girl or woman has had sexual intercourse
a surgical procedure to 'repair' or 'restore' the hymen, often linked to controlling women and girls

keyLearningPoints.keyLearningPoint: Virginity testing and hymenoplasty are harmful practices that violate rights and can cause physical and emotional harm.
Both practices are based on myths about virginity and female purity that have no medical or scientific basis.
It is a criminal offence to perform, assist in, or arrange virginity testing or hymenoplasty in the UK or abroad.
Failing to protect someone under 16 from these practices is also against the law.
Support and protection are available through trusted adults, schools, the NHS and helplines such as NSPCC or Childline.

misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.response: There is no medical test that can prove virginity. The hymen can stretch for many reasons.
misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.misconception: Virginity testing shows if someone has had sex or not.

lessons.pupilLessonOutcome: I can explain why virginity testing and hymenoplasty are harmful, illegal practices, and explain where to seek help and support.

teacherTips.teacherTip: Speak to your RSHE lead before teaching this lesson. When delivering the lesson, reinforce the key messages that these practices are harmful, illegal and never the victim’s fault. Be aware of the safeguarding and disclosure policies for your setting before teaching this lesson.

Hello, my name's Ms. Wellow and I'm going to be your teacher for today's lesson.
Today's lesson is called hymenoplasty and virginity testing, and it fits into the unit, "Staying Safe and Healthy: Forced Marriage, FGM, Hymenoplasty, and Virginity Testing".

If you don't have an adult with you at the moment, please come back to this lesson when you do have one with you.
If at any point during this lesson you do feel worried or uncomfortable, it's really important that you stop the lesson and that you speak to a trusted adult.
Okay, let's make a start.

Before we get started with today's lesson, we need to go over some ground rules.

When we disagree with someone else, it's important to challenge the statement and not the person themselves.
Next, Andeep says that we need to respect each other's privacy.
We can discuss examples, but we shouldn't use any names or descriptions that could identify anyone, including ourselves.
If we want to share a story or an experience, we can refer to someone as "my friend".
This means that we're not going to give away any identifying information.
Next, Jacob says, "No judgment.
We can explore any beliefs and misunderstandings that we have about a topic without fear of being judged by others." And finally, Izzy says that we can choose our level of participation.

lessons.unitTitle: Our changing bodies: What do I need to know about menstruation?

lessonKeywords.description: the blood-filled lining of the uterus which sheds every month there is no fertilised egg implanted
an organ, also called a womb, where a fertilised egg can grow into a foetus
one of two glands that contain and release egg cells
also called oviduct, one leads from each ovary to the uterus
fluid made in the cervix or vagina that helps to keep the vagina clean and moist

keyLearningPoints.keyLearningPoint: There are four phases in the menstrual cycle; the length of cycle depends on many factors.
Ovaries produce eggs which travel down the fallopian tubes to the womb or the uterus.
The endometrium thickens ready for a fertilised egg; when an egg isn’t fertilised, the endometrium is shed as a period.
Menstruation is different for all individuals and there is no ‘normal’.
People can track their menstrual cycles and that can be helpful for preparation.

misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.response: Cycles can vary in length between 21 and 45 days.  Cycles vary most when someone's periods have just started (the menarche) and when someone is approaching the menopause. Cycles can also vary, for example, because of stress.
misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.misconception: Normal cycles last 28 days.

lessons.pupilLessonOutcome: I can describe the menstrual cycle and explain how to track cycles.

teacherTips.teacherTip: Consider discussing one interpretation of the Ishango Bone with the class which suggests it is the earliest known period tracker!
